records.themeTitle: A commemorated miracle identifies an enduring repair
records.themeSummary: The oil points to the Torah illumination restored through Chanukah, beyond the immediate ability to perform one commandment.
records.originHebrew: לְהָבִין לָמָּה הֻצְרַךְ הַנֵּס בַּחֲנֻכָּה בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמְּנוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא רַק לְקַיֵּם מִצְוָה אַחַת, אֲשֶׁר גַּם בְּלֹא זֶה "אֹנֶס רַחֲמָנָא פַּטְרֵיהּ". אָמְנָם כִּי הָיָה זֶה מְרַמֵּז עַל אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה שֶׁנִּשְׁפַּע אָז דַּוְקָא, מַה שֶּׁרָצוּ הַיְּוָנִים "לְהַשְׁכִּיחָם תּוֹרָתֶךָ".
records.originEnglish: To understand why Chanukah required a miracle in the menorah’s oil, which served only to fulfill one commandment, when even without it ‘the Merciful One exempts a person prevented by circumstances.’ Rather, this indicated the light of holy Torah bestowed specifically then, which the Greeks had sought to make them forget—‘Your Torah.’
records.targetHebrew: עִנְיַן מִצְוַת נֵר חֲנֻכָּה לְזֵכֶר נֵס דַּחֲנֻכָּה, וּבֶאֱמֶת עִיקַּר הַנֵּס הָיָה הַצָּלָתָם מִשְּׁמַד הַיְּוָנִים, וְהַנֵּס דְּשֶׁמֶן זֶה הָיָה אַחַר כָּךְ עִנְיָן בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ, דִּלְכָאוֹרָה אֵין לוֹ שַׁיָּיכוּת לְגוּף יְשׁוּעַת הַהַצָּלָה שֶׁהוּא הָעִיקָּר. וּבְנוּסַח "עַל הַנִּסִּים" לֹא נִזְכַּר כְּלַל נֵס זֶה שֶׁהָיָה בַּשֶּׁמֶן, רַק דְּ"אַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ" וְכוּלֵי "וְהִדְלִיקוּ נֵרוֹת". אֲבָל כָּל יְשׁוּעָה שֶׁנִּקְבַּע מִמֶּנָּה זֵכֶר לְדוֹרוֹת, הַיְינוּ שֶׁכְּבָר נוֹשְׁעוּ הַנְּפָשׁוֹת דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם אֵיזֶה חִסָּרוֹן מַה, דְּמַחֲמָתוֹ הָיָה הַגְּזֵירוֹת וְהַצָּרוֹת מִקּוֹדֶם, דְּהַכֹּל בְּמִשְׁפָּט. וּכְשֶׁנִּתְעוֹרְרוּ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לְתַקֵּן לְאוֹתוֹ הַחִסָּרוֹן בִּלְבָבָם, אָז נוֹשְׁעוּ מֵהַצָּרָה. וְכַאֲשֶׁר תִּיקְּנוּ לְגַמְרֵי אוֹתוֹ עִנְיָן עַד הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁל כְּלָלוּת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, בְּעִנְיָן שֶׁמֵּהַיּוֹם וָהֵילָךְ כָּל נְפָשׁוֹת דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם מְתוּקָּנִים בִּפְרָט זֶה, אָז נִקְבְּעָה יְשׁוּעָה זוֹ זֵכֶר לְדוֹרוֹת. וְקָבְעוּ אֵיזֶה מִצְוָה לִהְיוֹת לְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן, לְהַמְשִׁיךְ עֲלֵיהֶם קְדֻשַּׁת תִּיקּוּן זֶה. דְּכָל דָּבָר שֶׁל קְדֻשָּׁה אֵין בָּא בְּעַצְמוֹ לַלֵּב אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי אֵיזֶה אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא וּפְתִיחָה כְּחֻדָּהּ שֶׁל מַחַט מִלְּמַטָּה, וְקָבְעוּ מִצְוָה הָרְאוּיָה לִפְתִיחַת אוֹתוֹ הָאוֹר וְהַקְּדֻשָּׁה בַּלֵּב.
records.targetEnglish: The commandment of the Chanukah lamp commemorates Chanukah’s miracle. In truth, the principal miracle was rescue from the Greeks’ persecution of the faith; the oil miracle happened afterwards as a separate matter, apparently unrelated to the essential rescue. The text of Al HaNissim does not mention this oil miracle at all, only that afterwards they came and lit lamps. But any deliverance from which a memorial is established for the generations means that Israel’s souls have already been delivered concerning the deficiency that had brought the decrees and troubles beforehand, for everything is in judgment. When Israel awakened to repair that deficiency within their hearts, they were delivered from the trouble. When they repaired the matter completely, as far as the root of the entire congregation of Israel, so that henceforth all Israel’s souls are repaired in this particular respect, that deliverance was established as a memorial for the generations. A commandment was instituted as an awakening from below at that season, to draw the holiness of this repair upon them. No holy thing comes into the heart by itself, but through some awakening from below, an opening below as small as the eye of a needle. They therefore established the commandment suited to opening this light and holiness in the heart.
records.explanation: Resisei explains why commemorating the oil is more than preserving an optional rescue of a ritual performance: the selected mitzvah reopens the particular inward repair that outlasts the event. This gives a reason for the oil’s role as Torah illumination in Rav Tzadok’s opening question. The causal account of the historical trouble is the author’s theological interpretation.

records.themeTitle: The patriarchs’ acquired holiness becomes inheritance
records.themeSummary: The holy qualities named through the shepherds belong within Israel’s souls, rather than remaining qualities of distant exemplary figures alone.
records.originHebrew: כַּיָּדוּעַ כִּי יֵשׁ שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת בִּקְדֻשָּׁה שֶׁהֵם קְדֻשַּׁת הַשִּׁבְעָה רוֹעִים שֶׁהֵם מֶרְכָּבָה לָהֶם, וּקְדֻשָּׁתָם נִמְצָא בִּכְלַל נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל: כִּי שָׁלֹשׁ מִדּוֹת הָאָבוֹת הַקְּדוֹשִׁים נִמְצָא בִּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהֵם רַחֲמָנִים, בַּיְּשָׁנִין, וְגוֹמְלֵי חֲסָדִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יְבָמוֹת ע״ט עַמּוּד א׳); וּמִדּוֹת מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן הֵם בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, וְנִמְצָא בִּכְלַל יִשְׂרָאֵל; וּמִדַּת יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁהָיָה מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק, וּכְתִיב: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים", וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים עַל שְׁמוֹ "שְׁאֵרִית יוֹסֵף"; וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּחִינַת מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם, כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
records.originEnglish: There are seven attributes in holiness, the holiness of the seven shepherds who are a vehicle for them, and their holiness is present throughout Israel’s souls. The three attributes of the holy patriarchs are found throughout Israel: compassionate, bashful, and performers of kindness. Moses’ and Aaron’s attributes are Written Torah and Oral Torah, which are found throughout Israel. Joseph the righteous was a vehicle for the attribute of the righteous one; it is written, ‘Your people are all righteous,’ and all Israel is called by his name, ‘the remnant of Joseph.’ King David represents heavenly kingship, the congregation of Israel.
records.targetHebrew: לָכֵן בִּיקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּעֲזוֹר לוֹ מֵהַקְּדוּשָּׁה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּתוֹלַדְתּוֹ שֶׁהִיא בִּבְחִינַת אֲחוֹתוֹ, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ שְׁמִירָה לְבַל יִמּוֹט חַס וְשָׁלוֹם. וְכָאן אַחַר אֲשֶׁר פָּעַל וְעָשָׂה חַיִל הַרְבֵּה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה עַל יְדֵי הַנִּסְיוֹנוֹת וּמַעֲשָׂיו הַטּוֹבִים עַד שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּלֵּם בְּמִצְוַת הַמִּילָה, הִתְפַּלֵּל לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁכָּל הַקְּדוּשָּׁה שֶׁקָּנָה עַד כֹּה תִּהְיֶה נִקְבַּעַת בּוֹ לִהְיוֹת בִּבְחִינַת אֲחוֹתִי, הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוּשָּׁה גַּם שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעַת, שֶׁלֹּא תּוּכַל לָבוֹא עוֹד לִידֵי הֶפְסֵד בְּשׁוּם אוֹפֶן, וְגַם אִם יִכָּנֵס בִּסְפֵיקוֹת וְהַסְתָּרוֹת, זֹאת הַקְּדוּשָּׁה לֹא תִּכְנוֹס לִסְפֵיקוֹת וְהוּא יַתְחִיל מֵחָדָשׁ לַעֲבוֹד אֶת ה' לִקְנוֹת יוֹתֵר קְדוּשָּׁה בִּיגִיעַ כַּפָּיו. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהֵם נִיכָּרִים בְּאֵלּוּ הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה סִימָנִים, שֶׁהֵם רַחְמָנִים בַּיְישָׁנִים גּוֹמְלֵי חֲסָדִים (יְבָמוֹת עט.), שֶׁהֵם נִקְבְּעוּ בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתוֹלָדָה מִיְּרוּשַּׁת הָאָבוֹת הַקְּדוֹשִׁים:
records.targetEnglish: Abraham therefore asked God to help him through the holiness present in his inborn nature, called ‘his sister,’ so that it would guard him from faltering, Heaven forbid. Here, after he had accomplished much in holiness through his trials and good deeds, reaching completion in circumcision, he prayed that all the holiness he had acquired until then should become fixed within him as ‘my sister’: that Israel should possess holiness even without conscious awareness, which could never be lost in any way. Even if he enters doubts and concealments, that holiness will not enter doubt, and he will begin anew to serve God and acquire more holiness through his own toil. As the Sages said, Israel is recognizable through these three signs—compassion, bashfulness, and kindness—which were fixed in Israel’s heart by birth as an inheritance from the holy patriarchs.
records.explanation: Beit Yaakov explains how the three ancestral qualities become a stable resource in later souls: holiness gained through the patriarch’s trials becomes inherited protection, while each descendant still has further work. The full preceding distinction between acquired “wife” and inborn “sister” holiness was read. This explains the collective presence of the qualities without implying that inherited holiness completes everyone’s practical service.

Clarified antecedents and grammatical referents are integrated into the English; original authorial asides remain explicit; the relation explanation is editorial and is not part of the quotation.

records.themeTitle: Oral Torah is inwardly acquired wisdom
records.themeSummary: The claim to possess the written text differs from Torah becoming the living wisdom of Israel’s heart.
records.originHebrew: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא כִּי תִשָּׂא ל״ד): לְפִי שֶׁצָּפָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁעֲתִידִים לְתַרְגֵּם הַתּוֹרָה יְוָנִית, וְהֵם אוֹמְרִים "אָנוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל" וְכוּלֵיהּ, "מִי שֶׁמִּסְטוֹרִין שֶׁלִּי אֶצְלוֹ הֵם בָּנַי", וְהַיְנוּ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּכוּת בָּהּ. כִּי עִקַּר חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה לִהְיוֹת נִקְבָּע הַחָכְמָה בַּלֵּב.
records.originEnglish: As the Tanchuma says: the Holy One foresaw that they would translate the Torah into Greek and say, ‘We are Israel.’ He answers, ‘Those with whom My hidden teachings are found are My children’—Oral Torah, in which they have no share. For the essence of the wisdom of Oral Torah is that wisdom becomes fixed in the heart.
records.targetRef: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 4:3
records.targetHebrew: וְהַיְינוּ כִּי "תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה" רָצָה לוֹמַר הַנּוֹבֵעַ מִן הַלֵּב יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר עַל מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (י״ט עַמּוּד א׳): בַּתְּחִלָּה "תּוֹרַת ה'", וּלְבַסּוֹף "תּוֹרָתוֹ"; שֶׁהַהַתְחָלָה הוּא תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִתְחִיל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא "דִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים", שֶׁלִּבּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם הַמַּמְצִיאִים אוֹתָהּ, וְהוּא תּוֹרָתָם לְבַד. וְזֶה עֵדוּת שֶׁהֵם בַּעֲלֵי הַתּוֹרָה וְלֹא אֲחֵרִים, שֶׁהוּא שֶׁלָּהֶם בְּיִחוּד, וְאָז הוּא כִּלְיוֹן מַלְכוּת אֱדוֹם לְגַמְרֵי הַטּוֹעֲנִים כָּךְ.
records.targetEnglish: ‘Oral Torah’ means what springs from Israel’s heart. As I explained elsewhere concerning the Sages’ statement: at first it is ‘the Torah of the Lord,’ and afterwards ‘his Torah.’ The beginning is Written Torah; afterwards Oral Torah began. It is called ‘the words of the scribes,’ for Israel’s hearts bring it forth, and it is their Torah alone. This testifies that they, rather than others, are the Torah’s owners, that it belongs particularly to them. This then brings the complete end of Edom’s kingdom, which makes that claim.
records.explanation: Ohr Zarua spells out the decisive word “in the heart”: Torah becomes an inwardly acquired and generative possession, expressed by “his Torah.” It addresses the same claim to Israel’s identity, rather than merely sharing a general praise of oral teaching. The full target places the argument within its polemic about Edom; that setting remains distinct from the origin’s Greek translation.

records.themeTitle: Rachel’s descendants answer opposition through disciplined work
records.themeSummary: The mention of Joseph’s line is illuminated by the sustained service represented by Rachel’s descendants.
records.originHebrew: וֶאֱדוֹם נוֹפֵל בְּיַד בָּנֶיהָ שֶׁל רָחֵל, וְהַיְנוּ שֵׁבֶט יוֹסֵף שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן מִדָּה הַשִּׁשִּׁית. וְגוֹג וּמָגוֹג נוֹפֵל בְּיַד מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד, בְּחִינַת מִדָּה הַשְּׁבִיעִית.
records.originEnglish: Edom falls through Rachel’s descendants—that is, Joseph’s tribe, which is likewise the sixth attribute. Gog and Magog fall through Messiah son of David, the seventh attribute.
records.targetHebrew: וזהו נמי שאמרו ז"ל בגמ' (ב"ב קכג) גמירי שאין עמלק נופל אלא ביד בניה של רחל היינו כי בניה של רחל מורה על התגברות עבודה בגודל צמצומים ולזה טרם שנגמר השלימות ממלכות בית דוד ואז התיצב נגדם עמלק לכך היו צריכין נגדו מלך מבני רחל וכן מצינו גבי משה רבינו ויקח משה את עצמות יוסף עמו ועצמות יוסף רומזים על גודל צמצומים והוא יען שהיו ישראל עדיין משוללי שלימות כמו שהי' אז קטרוג ביציאתם ממצרים הללו וכו' והללו וכו' אלא שהשי"ת העיד עליהם כדכתיב בהוציאך את העם ממצרים תעבדון את האלהים וגו' וכל עוד שישראל נוסעים בדרך לקנות שלימות טרם שמגיעים לזאת השלימות בזה הדרך מתיצב תמיד נגדם עמלק בקטרוגו כמו שנאמר אשר קרך בדרך וגו' ואז הוא כל העצה נגדו רק עצמות יוסף היינו התגברות עבודה כי אם ינוחו מעט אזי הוא מטעה תיכף בקטרוגו
records.targetEnglish: This is also the Sages’ statement: it is received as tradition that Amalek falls only through Rachel’s descendants. Rachel’s descendants indicate intensified service through great self-restraint. Thus, before the completeness of David’s kingship had been achieved, when Amalek stood against them, they needed a king from Rachel’s descendants. So too, ‘Moses took Joseph’s bones with him’: Joseph’s bones indicate great self-restraint. Israel had not yet attained completeness, and the accusation remained at their departure from Egypt, ‘These served idols, and those served idols.’ God nevertheless testified for them: ‘When you bring the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God.’ As long as Israel travels the road toward acquiring completeness, before reaching it, Amalek stands along that road in accusation—‘who encountered you on the road.’ The only counsel against him then is Joseph’s bones, intensified service. If they rest even a little, he immediately misleads through his accusation.
records.explanation: Sod explains the spiritual function associated with Rachel’s descendants: persistent, bounded service while completeness has not yet arrived. Its immediate application is to Amalek, a narrower scope than Rav Tzadok’s opening reference to Edom; it is not presented as a new proof that the two terms are interchangeable. It explains why Joseph’s line is assigned the opposing role.

records.themeTitle: Greater Torah wisdom produces greater humility
records.themeSummary: Humility follows from recognizing the source of one’s wisdom; it is the intended result of Torah entering the heart.
records.originHebrew: וְזָכַר בַּגְּמָרָא "שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בוֹעֵט וְכוּלֵיהּ", שֶׁזֶּה תַּכְלִית הַמְּכֻוָּן שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה: לִהְיוֹת רוּחוֹ שְׁפָלָה עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה, וְלֹא יִהְיֶה בוֹעֵט בְּמִי שֶׁגָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ. וְלָכֵן נִמְצָא תַּכְלִית הַשִּׁפְלוּת בַּתּוֹרָה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה בַּנְּפָשׁוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ שֶׁל חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה: דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר: "וְאָנֹכִי עָפָר וָאֵפֶר", וְאָמְרוּ עָלָיו (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס״א) שֶׁזִּמֵּן לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שְׁנֵי כִלְיוֹתָיו כְּמִין שְׁנֵי רַבָּנִים וְהָיוּ נוֹבְעוֹת וּמְלַמְּדוֹת אוֹתוֹ תּוֹרָה; וּבְמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "וְנַחְנוּ מָה", וְהֵמָּה הָיוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה; וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁאָמַר: "וְאָנֹכִי תוֹלַעַת", וְהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כִּי הוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת, "פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה". וְהַיְנוּ כִּי עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנִּקְבַּע הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּלִבָּם, מִזֶּה דַּוְקָא בָּאוּ לְתַכְלִית הַשִּׁפְלוּת בְּנַפְשָׁם;
records.originEnglish: The Talmud mentions ‘that he should not kick against those greater than him’ because this is Torah’s intended purpose: that through Torah his spirit should become lowly, and he should not kick against someone greater. Thus the holy Torah’s utmost humility appears in those souls who were the roots of Torah wisdom. Abraham said, ‘I am dust and ashes,’ and the Sages said that God supplied him with his two kidneys as two teachers, which flowed and taught him Torah. Moses and Aaron said, ‘What are we?’ and they were the roots of Written and Oral Torah. King David said, ‘I am a worm’; he too is a root of Oral Torah, being a vehicle for kingship—‘the mouth, Oral Torah.’ Precisely because words of Torah became fixed in their hearts, they reached the utmost lowliness within their souls.
records.targetHebrew: מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּחָכְמַת הָאֱמֶת, שֶׁהִיא חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה, כָּל מַה שֶּׁמּוֹסִיף חָכְמָה מוֹסִיף עֲנָוָה וְשִׁפְלוּת רוּחַ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק ו׳), כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, רַבָּן שֶׁל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל, הָיָה עָנָו מִכָּל הָאָדָם, כִּי כָּל חָכְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא לְהַכִּיר שֶׁ"אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ" וְשֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּמִמֵּילָא מַכִּיר שִׁפְלוּתוֹ וְאֵין לוֹ בַּמֶּה לְהִתְגָּאוֹת כְּלָל;
records.targetEnglish: In true wisdom, the wisdom of Torah, the more one adds wisdom, the more one adds humility and lowliness of spirit, as Avot says. Moses, the teacher of all Israel, was more humble than every person. All Israel’s wisdom is to recognize that ‘there is nothing besides Him’ and that everything comes from God. One consequently recognizes his own lowliness and has nothing at all in which to take pride.
records.explanation: Divrei gives the causal explanation for the origin’s examples: wisdom discloses dependence on God rather than an independent possession in which to boast. Humility is therefore a consequence of the wisdom’s content, not a decorative trait added to scholarship.

records.themeTitle: Greater Torah wisdom produces greater humility
records.themeSummary: Humility follows from recognizing the source of one’s wisdom; it is the intended result of Torah entering the heart.
records.originHebrew: וְזָכַר בַּגְּמָרָא "שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא בוֹעֵט וְכוּלֵיהּ", שֶׁזֶּה תַּכְלִית הַמְּכֻוָּן שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה: לִהְיוֹת רוּחוֹ שְׁפָלָה עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה, וְלֹא יִהְיֶה בוֹעֵט בְּמִי שֶׁגָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ. וְלָכֵן נִמְצָא תַּכְלִית הַשִּׁפְלוּת בַּתּוֹרָה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה בַּנְּפָשׁוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ שֶׁל חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה: דְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אָמַר: "וְאָנֹכִי עָפָר וָאֵפֶר", וְאָמְרוּ עָלָיו (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס״א) שֶׁזִּמֵּן לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שְׁנֵי כִלְיוֹתָיו כְּמִין שְׁנֵי רַבָּנִים וְהָיוּ נוֹבְעוֹת וּמְלַמְּדוֹת אוֹתוֹ תּוֹרָה; וּבְמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "וְנַחְנוּ מָה", וְהֵמָּה הָיוּ שֹׁרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה; וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁאָמַר: "וְאָנֹכִי תוֹלַעַת", וְהוּא שֹׁרֶשׁ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה כִּי הוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת, "פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה". וְהַיְנוּ כִּי עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנִּקְבַּע הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּלִבָּם, מִזֶּה דַּוְקָא בָּאוּ לְתַכְלִית הַשִּׁפְלוּת בְּנַפְשָׁם;
records.originEnglish: The Talmud mentions ‘that he should not kick against those greater than him’ because this is Torah’s intended purpose: that through Torah his spirit should become lowly, and he should not kick against someone greater. Thus the holy Torah’s utmost humility appears in those souls who were the roots of Torah wisdom. Abraham said, ‘I am dust and ashes,’ and the Sages said that God supplied him with his two kidneys as two teachers, which flowed and taught him Torah. Moses and Aaron said, ‘What are we?’ and they were the roots of Written and Oral Torah. King David said, ‘I am a worm’; he too is a root of Oral Torah, being a vehicle for kingship—‘the mouth, Oral Torah.’ Precisely because words of Torah became fixed in their hearts, they reached the utmost lowliness within their souls.
records.targetHebrew: וכמו שמצינו גבי משה רבינו שנאמר עליו והאיש משה עניו מאד וגו' והלא באמת ידע מ"ר בטח שהוא הגדול מכל ישראל כי הוא בעצמו כתב התורה מפי הקב"ה הנאמר בה ולא קם נביא וגו' הרי שידע שפיר שהוא הגדול אלא שהכיר היטב שאין באמת שום כח הויה בעולם זולת השי"ת כי אין עוד מלבדו ומאחר שהיה מכיר כ"כ היטב לזה היה הוא הכלי קיבול לקבל כל מיני אורות מהשי"ת כי הכיר היטב שכל אותו הגדלות שיש בו אינו מצדו כלל רק מצד השי"ת שבחר בו וכך אם היה בוחר בנפש אחר מישראל היה יכול להיות הנפש האחר הגדול והמובחר מכל ישראל ועל זאת ההכרה נאמר והאיש משה עניו מאד וגו' ולזה היה הוא הכלי לקבל כל מיני אורות
records.targetEnglish: Thus concerning Moses it says, ‘The man Moses was exceedingly humble.’ Surely Moses knew that he was the greatest of all Israel: he himself wrote the Torah from the Holy One’s mouth, including ‘No prophet arose again like Moses.’ He therefore knew very well that he was the greatest. Rather, he clearly recognized that no power of existence is present in the world apart from God, for there is nothing besides Him. Because he recognized this so clearly, he was the receptive vessel for every kind of divine light. He knew that all the greatness within him was not from himself at all, but from God, who chose him. Had God chosen another soul of Israel, that other soul could have been the greatest and most distinguished of all Israel. Of this recognition it says, ‘The man Moses was exceedingly humble.’ This is why he was the vessel to receive every kind of light.
records.explanation: Sod resolves a possible misunderstanding of the humility Rav Tzadok praises: Moses did not falsely deny his actual stature. He accurately distinguished the gift from independent self-importance. The full target uses this as the model for the High Priest’s receptivity, making the comparison specifically about wisdom and inward posture.

records.themeTitle: Reduced clarity can require deeper Torah labor
records.themeSummary: The diminished heart does not end Torah; the effort demanded by concealment can reveal a light able to reach within it.
records.originHebrew: אָמְנָם בָּזֶה דַּוְקָא אָז הָיָה הַנֵּס בַּשֶּׁמֶן, הַמְּרַמֵּז לִבְחִינַת חָכְמָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מְנָחוֹת פ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳): "מַאי שְׁנָא תְּקוֹעַ? מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁרְגִילִין בְּשֶׁמֶן זַיִת חָכְמָה מְצוּיָה בָּהֶן". וְנִתְבָּרֵךְ הַמּוּעָט לְהָאִיר אֶת הַחֹשֶׁךְ דַּוְקָא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תַּנְחוּמָא נֹחַ ג׳) עַל הַפָּסוּק "הָעָם הַהֹלְכִים בַּחֹשֶׁךְ רָאוּ אוֹר גָּדוֹל": אוֹר שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁגְּנָזוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְעַמְלֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וְכוּלֵיהּ; שֶׁדַּוְקָא עַל יְדֵי הַחֲשֵׁכוּת מְיַגְּעִים עַצְמָם בְּיוֹתֵר, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְרַבָּה הָאוֹר בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת; וּכְמוֹ כֵן בְּכָל דּוֹר דִּבְצַר לִבָּא בְּיוֹתֵר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֵירוּבִין נ״ג עַמּוּד א׳): "לִבָּם שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹנִים כְּפִתְחוֹ שֶׁל אוּלָם וְכוּלֵיהּ וְאָנוּ כִּמְלֹא נֶקֶב מַחַט סִדְקִית", וְדַוְקָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה עוֹד נִתְרַבָּה וְנִתְחַדֵּשׁ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה עַד אֵין שִׁעוּר.
records.originEnglish: Precisely in this situation the miracle occurred in oil, which indicates wisdom, as the Sages said concerning Tekoa: because they regularly use olive oil, wisdom is found among them. The small quantity was blessed to illuminate the darkness specifically. On ‘The people walking in darkness saw a great light,’ the Tanchuma says that the light created on the first day was hidden for those who toil in Oral Torah. Precisely through the darkness they exert themselves more, and thereby the light increases with greater strength. So too in every generation in which the heart diminishes further, as the Sages said, ‘The heart of the earlier ones was like the entrance of the Temple hall … and ours like the eye of a fine needle.’ Precisely through this, Oral Torah increases and is renewed beyond measure.
records.targetHebrew: וְדָבָר זֶה הוּא עֲשִׁירוּת שֶׁל חָכְמָה מְרֻבָּה יוֹתֵר, שֶׁעִקַּר עָמְקָהּ שֶׁל חָכְמָה בַּחֲרִיפוּת וְחִדּוּד הֲלָכָה הוּא עַל יְדֵי זֶה, וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חָדֵי בְּפִלְפּוּלָא; וְדָבָר זֶה בָּא מִתּוֹךְ הַהֶעְלֵם שֶׁאֵין הָאוֹר בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת, דְּאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּתַנְחוּמָא [נֹחַ ג׳] עַל פָּסוּק: "הָעָם הַהֹלְכִים בַּחֹשֶׁךְ רָאוּ אוֹר גָּדוֹל" [יְשַׁעְיָהוּ ט׳:א׳] — עַל חָכְמַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה; וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (כ״ד עַמּוּד א׳) עַל פָּסוּק: "בְּמַחֲשַׁכִּים הוֹשִׁיבַנִי [כִּמְתֵי עוֹלָם]" [אֵיכָה ג׳:ו׳] — זוֹ תַּלְמוּדָהּ שֶׁל בָּבֶל, שֶׁשָּׁם הָיָה הִתְגַּלּוּת עֹמֶק הַפִּלְפּוּל. דְּדָבָר זֶה גָּרַם גַּם כֵּן גָּלוּת בָּבֶל, דְּעַל יְדֵי הַגָּלוּת וְהַחֻרְבָּן נִסְתַּלֵּק הִתְגַּלּוּת הָאוֹר וְנִפְסְקָה הַנְּבוּאָה, דְּמִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ: הַט אָזְנְךָ וּשְׁמַע דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים [מִשְׁלֵי כ״ב:י״ז], כְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵדֶר עוֹלָם [פֶּרֶק ל׳]; וּכְמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּרֵישׁ אָבוֹת (פֶּרֶק א׳ מִשְׁנָה א׳) דִּנְבִיאִים מְסָרוּהָ לְאַנְשֵׁי כְנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה, הַיְינוּ שֶׁמָּסְרוּ הַשָּׂגַת הַתּוֹרָה לַחֲכָמִים, דְּרָאשֵׁיהֶם הוּא אַנְשֵׁי כְנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה, שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ כֵן עַל שֶׁהֶחֱזִירוּ עֲטָרָה לְיָשְׁנָהּ בַּאֲמִירַת "הַגָּדוֹל הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא", כְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹמָא (ס״ט עַמּוּד ב׳); הַיְינוּ דְּמִצַּד הַשָּׂגַת הַנְּבוּאָה שֶׁהוּא בְּהִתְגַּלּוּת, הֲרֵי בַּהַגָּלוּת מִצַּד הַהִתְגַּלּוּת הוּא בְּהֵיפֶךְ; אַךְ מִצַּד הַחָכְמָה דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, שֶׁהִיא הַמְגַלָּה הַמִּסְטוֹרִין דְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, כְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה מ״ז [מ״ז:א׳]): מִי שֶׁמִּסְטוֹרִין שֶׁלִּי בְּיָדוֹ וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁהוּא נֶעְלָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, רַק מִי שֶׁזּוֹכִין לַעֲמֹד עַל הַמִּסְטוֹרִין וְהַהֶעְלֵם, וְהַשָּׂגַת הָאוֹר מִתּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ דַּוְקָא, הֵם מַשִּׂיגִים דְּאַדְּרַבָּה, הֵן הֵן גְּבוּרוֹתָיו וּגְדֻלָּתוֹ וְנוֹרְאוֹתָיו, שֶׁגַּם בַּגָּלוּת וּבַחֹשֶׁךְ ה' אוֹר לָנוּ [מִיכָה ז׳:ח׳], וְהָאוֹר שֶׁמִּתּוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ הוּא אוֹר גָּדוֹל יוֹתֵר, שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהָאִיר גַּם בְּתוֹךְ הַחֹשֶׁךְ.
records.targetEnglish: This is a greater wealth of wisdom, for the principal depth of wisdom in incisive understanding and sharpening of halakhah comes through this, and the Holy One delights in dialectical study. This arises from concealment, when the light is not openly disclosed. The Tanchuma applies ‘The people walking in darkness saw a great light’ to the wisdom of Oral Torah. Sanhedrin likewise interprets ‘He has placed me in dark places’ as the Babylonian Talmud, where the depth of dialectical study was revealed. The Babylonian exile brought this about too: through exile and destruction, disclosed light departed and prophecy ceased. From then on, ‘Incline your ear and hear the words of the sages,’ as Seder Olam says. Avot says that the prophets transmitted it to the Men of the Great Assembly: they transmitted apprehension of Torah to the sages, headed by the Great Assembly. They were named for restoring the crown to its former state by saying ‘the great, mighty, and awesome,’ as Yoma explains. From the perspective of prophecy, which is disclosure, exile visibly shows the opposite. But Oral Torah’s wisdom reveals Written Torah’s hidden teachings, concealed in this world. Those who merit to grasp the hidden teaching and attain the light specifically from darkness recognize that these are, on the contrary, His might, greatness, and awesomeness: even in exile and darkness, the Lord is our light. The light from darkness is greater, for it can illuminate even within darkness.
records.explanation: Poked explains what “more light” means here: the wisdom can recognize divine presence under conditions in which the earlier kind of visible disclosure is absent. It does not simply declare every later sage greater than every earlier one. The complete paragraph’s account of toil, fear, and human choice was read.

records.themeTitle: Failure is repaired through the Torah it makes necessary
records.themeSummary: A failure can disclose the need for distinctions and disciplined service that were not previously understood.
records.originHebrew: אָמְנָם בָּזֶה דַּוְקָא אָז הָיָה הַנֵּס בַּשֶּׁמֶן, הַמְּרַמֵּז לִבְחִינַת חָכְמָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מְנָחוֹת פ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳): "מַאי שְׁנָא תְּקוֹעַ? מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁרְגִילִין בְּשֶׁמֶן זַיִת חָכְמָה מְצוּיָה בָּהֶן". וְנִתְבָּרֵךְ הַמּוּעָט לְהָאִיר אֶת הַחֹשֶׁךְ דַּוְקָא, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תַּנְחוּמָא נֹחַ ג׳) עַל הַפָּסוּק "הָעָם הַהֹלְכִים בַּחֹשֶׁךְ רָאוּ אוֹר גָּדוֹל": אוֹר שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁגְּנָזוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְעַמְלֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה וְכוּלֵיהּ; שֶׁדַּוְקָא עַל יְדֵי הַחֲשֵׁכוּת מְיַגְּעִים עַצְמָם בְּיוֹתֵר, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְרַבָּה הָאוֹר בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת; וּכְמוֹ כֵן בְּכָל דּוֹר דִּבְצַר לִבָּא בְּיוֹתֵר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֵירוּבִין נ״ג עַמּוּד א׳): "לִבָּם שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹנִים כְּפִתְחוֹ שֶׁל אוּלָם וְכוּלֵיהּ וְאָנוּ כִּמְלֹא נֶקֶב מַחַט סִדְקִית", וְדַוְקָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה עוֹד נִתְרַבָּה וְנִתְחַדֵּשׁ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה עַד אֵין שִׁעוּר.
records.originEnglish: Precisely in this situation the miracle occurred in oil, which indicates wisdom, as the Sages said concerning Tekoa: because they regularly use olive oil, wisdom is found among them. The small quantity was blessed to illuminate the darkness specifically. On ‘The people walking in darkness saw a great light,’ the Tanchuma says that the light created on the first day was hidden for those who toil in Oral Torah. Precisely through the darkness they exert themselves more, and thereby the light increases with greater strength. So too in every generation in which the heart diminishes further, as the Sages said, ‘The heart of the earlier ones was like the entrance of the Temple hall … and ours like the eye of a fine needle.’ Precisely through this, Oral Torah increases and is renewed beyond measure.
records.targetHebrew: ואיתא בש"ס (בכורות ה:) מה רפידים שריפו עצמן מן דברי תורה. והענין הכשלון הזה שהיה קודם מתן תורה שבזה הראה להם השי"ת, שכל מיני כשלונות שנמצא לפעמים אצל ישראל ע"י דברי תורה יוכלו לתקן הכל. וכמו שאנו רואים שיש כמה וכמה דברי תורה שלא יכול האדם לבוא עליהם בלתי הכשלון שמקודם, כמו שאיתא בש"ס (גיטין מג.) על הפסוק (ישעיהו ג׳:ו׳) והמכשלה הזאת תחת ידך, אין אדם עומד על ד"ת אלא א"כ נכשל בהן. ובזאת הראה להם השי"ת שע"י דברי תורה יוכלו לתקן הכל.
records.targetEnglish: The Talmud says, ‘What is Rephidim? They became slack in words of Torah.’ The meaning of this failure before the giving of the Torah is that God showed them that all the failures which sometimes occur in Israel can be repaired through words of Torah. As we see, there are many matters of Torah that a person cannot attain without the preceding failure. Thus the Talmud says on ‘This stumbling block is under your hand’: a person does not grasp words of Torah unless he has first stumbled in them. Through this God showed them that they could repair everything through words of Torah.
records.explanation: The full Tiferet paragraph identifies the error concretely: treating divine initiative as a reason to abandon service, then repairing that separation through Torah and safeguards. This illuminates how the origin’s diminished heart can lead to more exact Torah work. It is not advice to seek failure or an assertion that failure by itself produces wisdom.
records.translationProvenance: English quotations translated or checked anew against the exact canonical Hebrew during the Chanukah review. Clarified antecedents and grammatical referents are integrated into the English; original authorial asides remain explicit; the relation explanation is editorial and is not part of the quotation.

records.themeTitle: Recognizing the source transforms a misdirected power
records.themeSummary: The phrase “everything is His” concerns the repair of imagination and desire through recognition and Torah, while practical wrongdoing still requires restraint.
records.originHebrew: וְזֶהוּ הָעִנְיָן שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "אֶשְׁכּוֹל מִי שֶׁהַכֹּל שֶׁלּוֹ", הַיְנוּ בּוֹרֵא אֶת הַכֹּל, בְּחִינַת הָרָע כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, "מְכַפֵּר לִי עַל עֲוֹן גְּדִי" הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת הַחֹשֶׁךְ שֶׁל הַבְּרִיאָה, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נֶהְפָּךְ לְ"טוֹב מְאֹד". וְעַל זֶה רָמְזוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: שֶׁבָּטְלוּ הָאֶשְׁכּוֹלוֹת, שֶׁכָּל הָאֶשְׁכּוֹלוֹת שֶׁעָמְדוּ מִימוֹת מֹשֶׁה עַד שֶׁמֵּת יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר הָיוּ לְמֵדִין תּוֹרָה כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ, וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם כֹּחַ עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה לַהֲפֹךְ אֶת הָרָע שֶׁל הַבְּרִיאָה לְ"טוֹב מְאֹד" כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לוֹ בְּאוֹתוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה: "וְעַתָּה הַנִּיחָה לִּי", שֶׁהָיָה תָּלוּי בּוֹ. וְלָכֵן נִקְרְאוּ גַּם כֵּן בְּשֵׁם "אֶשְׁכּוֹלוֹת שֶׁהַכֹּל בּוֹ", שֶׁבִּיכָלְתָּם לַעֲשׂוֹת עַל יְדֵי תּוֹרָתָם בְּחִינַת "הַכֹּל" לְטוֹב מְאֹד.
records.originEnglish: This is the saying, ‘A cluster—the One to whom everything belongs’: the Creator of everything, including the aspect called evil just explained. ‘He atones for the sin of the kid’—the aspect of darkness in creation—so that it becomes ‘very good.’ This is what the Sages indicated when they said that the eshkolot ceased. All the eshkolot from Moses’ time until Yose ben Yoezer’s death learned Torah like Moses: through Torah they had the power to turn creation’s evil into ‘very good,’ like Moses, to whom God said at that event the calf, ‘Now leave Me alone,’ making it depend upon him. They too were therefore called eshkolot, ‘those containing everything’: through their Torah they could make the aspect of ‘everything’ become very good.
records.targetHebrew: כִּי כַּאֲשֶׁר מִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁגַּם בְּעֵת הַדִּמְיוֹן הוּא דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת, וְהוּא שָׂם אֶל לְבָבוֹ זֶה, לָדַעַת כִּי מֵאַיִן לוֹ כֹּחַ לַחְשׁוֹב וּלְהַרְהֵר שׁוּם דָּבָר אִם לֹא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִמֵּילָא נִתְתַּקֵּן הַדִּמְיוֹן, כִּדְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת פח:): "מִי שֶׁהַכֹּל שֶׁלּוֹ מְכַפֵּר לִי עַל עֲווֹן גְּדִי וְכוּלֵי", שֶׁמִּי שֶׁהַכֹּל שֶׁלּוֹ – כָּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים וְהַפְּעֻלּוֹת וְהַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת וְהָרְצוֹנוֹת, אִם כֵּן גַּם הֶעָווֹן הוּא שֶׁלּוֹ, וּמִמֵּילָא מְכַפֵּר וְכוּלֵי. וּבְכֹחַ הַמְדַמֶּה עַצְמוֹ שֶׁבּוֹ גּוֹבֵר הַדִּמְיוֹן, בְּכֹחַ זֶה עַצְמוֹ הוּא מִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו לְכַלּוֹתוֹ וּלְבַטְּלוֹ. וְנִמְצָא שֶׁמִּתְהַפֵּךְ לִהְיוֹת שׁוֹרֶשׁ עֲמָלֵק הָרוֹדֵף – נִרְדָּף מֵעַצְמוֹ; שֶׁמִּכְתָּב שֶׁכָּתַב "לִהְיוֹת הַיְּהוּדִים וְגוֹמֵר", נִתְהַפֵּךְ הַפֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁבֵּאֲרוּ בַּכְּתָבִים שְׁנִיִּים, הַכַּוָּנָה הָיָה שֶׁיִּשְׁלְטוּ בְּשׂוֹנְאֵיהֶם; וְהָעֵץ שֶׁהֵכִין לְמָרְדֳּכַי נִתְהַפֵּךְ שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ; הַיְינוּ דְּהַהִתְגַּבְּרוּת שֶׁל הַדִּמְיוֹן עַצְמוֹ נִתְהַפֵּךְ אַחַר כָּךְ, שֶׁנִּתְבָּרֵר שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה הִתְגַּבְּרוּת דִּמְיוֹן כּוֹזֵב כְּלָל, רַק דְּבַר אֱמֶת לַאֲמִיתּוֹ, כְּמוֹ דֶּרֶךְ מָשָׁל חֲלוֹמוֹת יוֹסֵף, שֶׁבִּשְׁעַת מַעֲשֶׂה הָיָה נִרְאֶה דִּמְיוֹן, וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּשֶׁרָאוּ שֶׁהָיָה כֵּן, הֲרֵי נִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה דִּמְיוֹן כְּלָל. וְזֶהוּ הַמָּשָׁל בַּנִּגְלֶה, וְיֵשׁ בָּזֶה הַרְבֵּה מַדְרֵגוֹת גָּבוֹהַּ עַל גָּבוֹהַּ בְּהַעֲלָאַת הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת וְהַדִּמְיוֹנוֹת וְתִיקּוּנָן לִהְיוֹת נַעֲשֶׂה מִדִּמְיוֹן – אֱמֶת. וְהָעִיקָּר רַק עַל יְדֵי הַהַכָּרָה הַבְּרוּרָה שֶׁ"אֵין עוֹד מִלְּבַדּוֹ" וְהַכֹּל שֶׁלּוֹ, וְכָל חָכְמַת אֱנוֹשׁ וְתַחְבּוּלוֹתָיו אֵינוֹ כְּלוּם. וְכָךְ הוּא בְּעֵת שִׁכְרוּתוֹ, שֶׁאָז אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם דַּעַת וְחָכְמָה כְּמוֹ כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּדַעְתּוֹ, כִּי רַק הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמּוֹלִיד בּוֹ עֵצָה וּמַחֲשָׁבָה וְרָצוֹן, מִמֵּילָא נִתְקָן הַכֹּל. – וְנֶאֱמַר עַל זֶה: "וְהָיָה בְּהָנִיחַ וְגוֹמֵר", כִּי מִקּוֹדֶם צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּבִיעוּר שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת רָעוֹת שֶׁבְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא יָבוֹא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לִידֵי אֵיזֶה עֲבֵירָה בַּפּוֹעַל וְלֹא לִידֵי הִרְהוּרֵי עֲבֵירָה שֶׁבְּהִתְגַּלּוּת לִבּוֹ; וּכְשֶׁנָּקִי מִזֶּה, אָז יִשְׁתַּדֵּל לִמְחוֹת מִקֶּרֶב לְבָבוֹ דִּמְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁל הֶבֶל].
records.targetEnglish: When it becomes clear that even at the time of imagination he is truly attached to God, and he takes this to heart—knowing that he has no power to think or contemplate anything except from God—the imagination is consequently repaired. As the Sages said, ‘The One to whom everything belongs atones for the sin of the kid’: everything belongs to Him, all deeds, actions, thoughts, and desires; therefore the sin too belongs to Him, and He consequently atones. With the very faculty of imagination in which fantasy grows strong, one prevails against it, to consume and annul it. Thus the root of Amalek, the pursuer, becomes pursued through itself. The document he wrote, ‘That the Jews should …,’ had its interpretation reversed in the second documents, revealing the intention that they should rule over their enemies; and the gallows prepared for Mordecai were turned against him. The apparent victory of imagination was afterwards reversed: it became clear that false imagination had not prevailed, but actual truth. Joseph’s dreams are an example: at the time they appeared imaginary; afterwards, when events occurred accordingly, it became clear that they had not been fantasy at all. This is the visible analogy. There are many levels, higher than one another, in elevating and repairing thoughts and imaginings so that imagination becomes truth. The essential thing is clear recognition that ‘there is nothing besides Him,’ that everything is His, and that human wisdom and schemes are nothing. So too in drunkenness, when one lacks the understanding and wisdom of sobriety: since it is God alone who brings forth counsel, thought, and desire within him, everything is thereby repaired. Concerning this it says, ‘When the Lord gives rest.’ First a person must labor to remove the seven evil qualities revealed in his heart, so that he should not come to an actual transgression, Heaven forbid, or to thoughts of transgression revealed in his heart. Once he is clean of this, he should then labor to erase vain imaginings from within his heart.
records.explanation: Resisei explains the same “everything is His / sin of the kid” homily through a specific power: imagination ceases to claim independence from its source and can be turned toward truth. Its concluding requirement to restrain actual transgression and revealed sinful intention is retained in the quotation. The account of providence does not license practical wrongdoing.

Clarified antecedents and grammatical referents are integrated into the English; original authorial asides remain explicit; the relation explanation is editorial and is not part of the quotation.

records.themeTitle: The good root does not cancel the obligation to serve
records.themeSummary: The assurance that creation belongs to God is held together with judgment and the person’s work.

records.originEnglish: This is the saying, ‘A cluster—the One to whom everything belongs’: the Creator of everything, including the aspect called evil just explained. ‘He atones for the sin of the kid’—the aspect of darkness in creation—so that it becomes ‘very good.’ This is what the Sages indicated when they said that the eshkolot ceased. All the eshkolot from Moses’ time until Yose ben Yoezer’s death learned Torah like Moses: through Torah they had the power to turn creation’s evil into ‘very good,’ like Moses, to whom God said at that event the calf, ‘Now leave Me alone,’ making it depend upon him. They too were therefore called eshkolot, ‘those containing everything’: through their Torah they could make the aspect of ‘everything’ become very good.
records.targetHebrew: ולחשך קרא לילה, דא יצחק, היינו שמראה דאית דין ואית דיין, היינו שלאדם יכול לדמות שמאחר שהיפך מרצון השי"ת אין ביכולת לעשות כלום, אין צריך כלל לעבודה. וזה מדת יצחק, שמראה דאית דין ואית דיין, היינו שמי שלא ילך בעבודה בזה ההסתר הוא יאבד לגמרי, ואע"פ שאפילו ממי שאינו הולך בעבודה עולה ג"כ כבודו ית', כדאיתא במדרש (שמות ז) שכשם שקילוסו של הקב"ה עולה לו מגן עדן מפי הצדיקים כך עולה מגיהנם מפי הרשעים וכו'. אך זה שבתפיסתו אינו רוצה לראות הכבוד שמים היוצא ממנו, תפיסתו יאבד לגמרי. וזה מורה שצריך להזכיר מדת יום בלילה ומדת ללילה ביום, היינו שלא ילך האדם רק בתקיפות של יום שזה נקרא בוקרא דאברהם, רק שיכליל גם מדת יצחק שרומז על יראה ופחד. וכן צריך ליכלול מדת יום בלילה, היינו שלא יהיה לאדם מזה הפחד התרשלות ח"ו בעבודה, ורק צריך ליכלול גם מדת יום שהוא בוקרא דאברהם, כי בודאי השי"ת יברר אותו לטוב, מאחר שמצידו הוא עובד בכל כחו:
records.targetEnglish: ‘He called darkness night’—this is Isaac. It means that he shows that there is judgment and a Judge. A person might imagine that since nothing can be done contrary to God’s will, no service is needed. Isaac’s attribute shows that there is judgment and a Judge: someone who does not walk in service within this concealment will be entirely lost. Although even one who does not serve gives rise to His honor—as the Midrash says, His praise rises from the righteous in Eden and from the wicked in Gehinnom—one who, within his perception, does not wish to see the honor of Heaven arising from him will lose that perception entirely. This is why one must mention day’s attribute at night and night’s attribute by day. One must not walk only in day’s assurance, Abraham’s morning, but include Isaac’s attribute of fear and awe. Likewise one must include day within night, so that fear should not cause slackness in service, Heaven forbid. One must also include day, Abraham’s morning: God will certainly clarify him for good, since from his own side he works with all his power.
records.explanation: Tiferet provides a necessary complement to the origin’s claim that evil can be turned to good: providential good and moral responsibility must be held together. It expressly rejects the conclusion that belonging to God makes effort unnecessary, and equally rejects despair that prevents effort. This illuminates the qualification implicit in repair “through their Torah.”

records.themeTitle: Torah words are not identical with inward Torah
records.themeSummary: A person can utter words that belong to Torah without possessing their inward meaning; the heart’s reception remains decisive.
records.originHebrew: וְזֶה הָיָה מִשּׁוּם דִּבְצַר לִבָּא מִצַּד הַקְּלִפָּה שֶׁל חָכְמַת יְוָנִית שֶׁהָיָה בְּלֹא לֵב, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה ב׳, ט׳): "יֵשׁ תּוֹרָה אַל תַּאֲמֵן", דִּכְתִיב: "בַּגּוֹיִם אֵין תּוֹרָה", וְהַיְנוּ כִּי הַחָכְמָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם הוּא מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ וְאֵינָהּ מוֹרָה לַלֵּב; מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁעִקַּר קִנְיָנָהּ הוּא בַּלֵּב, כְּמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וּבְלֵב כָּל חֲכַם לֵב נָתַתִּי חָכְמָה" (וְנִתְבָּאֵר רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיִּשְׁלַח). וְזֶהוּ עִנְיַן אָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה עַל הַיְּוָנִים שֶׁטִּמְּאוּ כָּל הַשְּׁמָנִים, וְהַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁהֶחְשִׁיכוּ עֵינֵיהֶם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
records.originEnglish: This occurred because the heart was diminished through the husk of Greek wisdom, which was without heart. As we explained concerning the Midrash, ‘If they say there is Torah among the nations, do not believe it,’ for ‘there is no Torah among the nations’: their wisdom is from the lips outward and does not instruct the heart. Torah’s wisdom is different; its essential acquisition is in the heart, as it says, ‘In the heart of every wise-hearted person I have placed wisdom.’ This is the meaning of the Sages’ statement that the Greeks defiled all the oils: the wisdom in the heart, for they darkened Israel’s eyes.
records.targetHebrew: כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת, הָאוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ תּוֹרָה בְּאֻמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים – אַל תַּאֲמֵן (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה אֵיכָה ב, ט), כִּי "לֹא עָשָׂה כֵן לְכָל גּוֹי" (תְּהִלִּים קמז, כ). אֲבָל מִכָּל מָקוֹם, הֲרֵי אֲפִילּוּ בְּתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב נִכְתַּב הַרְבֵּה דִּבְרֵי רִשְׁעֵי אֻמּוֹת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וְהֵם מִכְּלַל הַתּוֹרָה, וְכֵן בִּנְבִיאִים וּכְתוּבִים. וְהֵם עַצְמָם לֹא יָדְעוּ מַה הֵם מְדַבְּרִים, רַק הַנָּבִיא וְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּתוֹכָם יָדְעוּ שֶׁזֶּהוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְכָל כֹּחָם מִזֶּה; וּמִיָּד שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּ בִּלְעָם מִפִּיהֶם, נִתְבַּטְּלָה מַלְכוּתָם.
records.targetEnglish: In truth, if someone says that Torah exists among the idolatrous nations, do not believe him, as the Midrash says: ‘He has not done so for any nation.’ Nevertheless, even Written Torah contains many words spoken by wicked people of those nations, and they are part of Torah; so too in the Prophets and Writings. They themselves did not know what they were saying. Only the prophet and Israel among them knew that these were words of Torah, and all their power came from this. Once Israel drew what they had swallowed out of their mouths, their kingship was annulled.
records.explanation: Tzidkat answers an apparent textual counterexample to the origin’s distinction: the Torah can contain an outsider’s words without those words having become Torah in that speaker’s own conscious heart. The meaning recognized by the prophet is distinguished from the speaker’s awareness. This is the author’s account of Torah acquisition, not a new claim that identical vocabulary establishes identical inward knowledge.

records.targetHebrew: וַיְהִי כָל הָאָרֶץ שָׂפָה אֶחָת וּדְבָרִים אֲחָדִים. וְלֹא נֶאֱמַר לָשׁוֹן אֶחָד, כִּי עִיקַּר לָשׁוֹן הוּא לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ, כִּי לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ הוּא מִמַּה שֶּׁנִּטְבַּע בְּעוֹמֶק הַלֵּב וְנוֹבֵעַ מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ הַחַיִּים, וּשְׁאָר הַלְּשׁוֹנוֹת נִקְרָאִים לְשׁוֹן עִלְּגִים, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יְשַׁעְיָה לג, יט) "נִלְעַג לָשׁוֹן אֵין בִּינָה", הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ חַיִּים בְּלִבּוֹ כִּי בִּינָה הוּא בַּלֵּב; וְדוֹר הַפַּלָּגָה אַף שֶׁדִּבְּרוּ בִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם שֹׁרֶשׁ חַיִּים, רַק מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ הָיוּ מְדַבְּרִים בָּהּ, כְּמוֹ פִּטְפּוּט וְצִפְצוּף הָעוֹפוֹת וּשְׁאָר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים. וְכֵן בְּעִנְיַן הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁהִקְשׁוּ כָּל הַמְפָרְשִׁים לָמָּה לֹא מָצָאנוּ בְּקִלְלָתוֹ שֶׁיּוּטַל מִמֶּנּוּ לְשׁוֹנוֹ, אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת לֹא הָיָה לוֹ לָשׁוֹן בַּשֹּׁרֶשׁ מֵאַחַר שֶׁדִּבֵּר לְשׁוֹן הָרָע עַל בּוֹרְאוֹ, וְהָבֵן.
records.targetEnglish: ‘The whole earth had one lip and common words.’ It does not say ‘one tongue,’ for the essential tongue is the holy tongue: it comes from what is impressed in the depths of the heart and springs from the root of life. The other tongues are called a stammering tongue, as it says, ‘A stammering tongue, without understanding’—without a root of life in the heart, for understanding is in the heart. Although the generation of the dispersion spoke the holy tongue, they had no root of life; they spoke it only from the lips outward, like the chatter and chirping of birds and other living creatures. So too with the serpent: the commentators ask why its curse does not mention that its tongue was taken away. In truth it had no tongue at the root, since it spoke slander against its Creator. Understand this.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach uses the very “lips outward” distinction to show that even correctly formed sacred language can lack inward life. This directly illuminates Rav Tzadok’s contrast between verbal knowledge and wisdom acquired in the heart. The comparison is about the author’s spiritual account of speech, not a linguistic judgment about the expressive capacity of other languages.

records.themeTitle: Differing views can share one divine root
records.themeSummary: Unity is recovered by recognizing the distinct approaches to serving God, not by pretending that all minds have the same view.
records.originHebrew: וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה (חֲגִיגָה ג׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל הַפָּסוּק "דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים וְגוֹמֵר בַּעֲלֵי אֲסֻפּוֹת": "הַלָּלוּ מְטַמְּאִין וְהַלָּלוּ מְטַהֲרִין וְכוּלֵיהּ, כֻּלָּם נִתְּנוּ מֵרֹעֶה אֶחָד, אֵל אֶחָד נְתָנָן וְכוּלֵיהּ", הַיְנוּ שֶׁגַּם עַתָּה שֶׁנִּתְמַעֲטוּ הַלְּבָבוֹת, יֵשׁ בַּכֹּחַ לִהְיוֹת נִקְנֶה בַּלֵּב לְהִתְאַחֵד גַּם חִלּוּקֵי הַדֵּעוֹת לִהְיוֹת בְּחִינַת "כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה טוֹב מְאֹד". וּבָזֶה יֻנַּח הַדְּרָשׁ (חֻלִּין צ״ב עַמּוּד א׳): "'הִבְשִׁילוּ אַשְׁכְּלֹתֶיהָ עֲנָבִים' אֵלּוּ הַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁבְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר", וְגַם אָמְרוּ: "אֶשְׁכּוֹלוֹת אֵלּוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים וְכוּלֵיהּ, לִיבְעֵי רַחֲמֵי אִתְכַּלְיָא עַל עַלְיָא", שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת יֵשׁ בְּכָל דּוֹר מְצִיאוּת בְּחִינַת אֶשְׁכּוֹלוֹת כָּאָמוּר.
records.originEnglish: This is Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah’s saying on ‘The words of the sages … masters of assemblies’: ‘These declare impure and those declare pure … all were given by one Shepherd; one God gave them.’ Even now, when hearts have diminished, there is power for Torah to become acquired in the heart and for differing views too to become united in the quality of ‘everything He made was very good.’ This explains the interpretation, ‘Its clusters ripened into grapes’—the righteous of every generation. The Sages also said, ‘Clusters are Torah scholars … let the clusters pray for the leaves.’ In truth, the quality of eshkolot is present in every generation, as explained.
records.targetHebrew: וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הִבְדִּיל וְיָצַר נִבְרָאִים שׁוֹנִים, עַל כָּרְחֲךָ דְּיֵשׁ הַשָּׂגוֹת שׁוֹנוֹת וְנִבְדָּלוֹת לְקִלּוּסוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְכָל אַחַת אֱמֶת לְעַצְמָהּ וּבִמְקוֹמָהּ. וְזֶהוּ מִדָּתָן שֶׁל אָבוֹת, שֶׁאֵין כָּאן מַחֲלוֹקֶת בֶּאֱמֶת. כִּי מִדַּת אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק, שֶׁהֵן אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה כַּיָּדוּעַ, שְׁתֵּיהֶן אֱמֶת גַּם יַחַד, וְצָרִיךְ לְעָבְדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּשְׁתֵּיהֶן. וְכָל אַחַת אֱמֶת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ וּכְפִי מַדְרֵגָתָהּ, כְּמוֹ מַיִם עֶלְיוֹנִים וְתַחְתּוֹנִים וְרָקִיעַ הַמַּבְדִּיל, שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִשְׁנֵיהֶם מְצִיאוּת גָּמוּר, כָּל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹמוֹ. אֲבָל בַּבָּנִים אַחַר כָּךְ — רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר בַּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת — כְּבָר הָיוּ כָּל אֶחָד כָּלוּל מִשְּׁתֵּי הַמִּדּוֹת, אֶלָּא שֶׁבְּאֶחָד גּוֹבֵר מִדָּה זוֹ וּבְאֶחָד גּוֹבֵר זוֹ. וּמִזֶּה נִתְהַוָּה הַמַּחֲלוֹקֶת, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁעַל דָּבָר אֶחָד עַצְמוֹ זֶה יֹאמַר כָּךְ וְזֶה יֹאמַר כָּךְ. כִּי כְּבָר הֵם כֻּלָּם מְחֻבָּרִים וּמְיֻחָדִים יַחַד גַּם כֵּן בְּהִתְכַּלְלוּת, וּלְפִיכָךְ בָּא מִזֶּה שְׁפִיטָתָם עַל דָּבָר אֶחָד בְּחִלּוּף.
records.targetEnglish: Since God distinguished and created different creatures, there must be different and distinct apprehensions for His praise, each true in itself and in its place. This is the patriarchs’ quality: there is no actual conflict here. Abraham’s and Isaac’s attributes, love and fear, are both true together, and He must be served through both. Each is true in itself and according to its level, like upper and lower waters with the firmament dividing them, each fully existing in its own place. But among the children afterwards—that is, as these attributes spread—each already included both attributes, though one predominated in one person and the other in another. From this disagreement arose: concerning the same thing, one says this and another says that. They are already all connected and united through mutual inclusion, and this produces their differing judgments about the same thing.
records.explanation: Resisei explains how genuine differences can emerge from one source: the same attributes are included in different proportions, yielding different judgments. The full paragraph distinguishes this from hatred and expressly requires love of one’s fellow. Thus the origin’s unity of differing views is not a refusal to recognize disagreement or a blanket approval of hostility.

records.targetHebrew: והנה כל זמן שאדם מכיר שהמדות האלה הציב השי"ת לטובת האדם, כדי שיהיה מקום לעבודת האדם, ומכיר שאין שום מקום אצלו שיהיה כ"כ נתרחק מאור ד' שלא יוכל להחזירו להשי"ת, ואז נקרא עדיין מחלוקת לשם שמים. וזה מורה מאמר הזוה"ק ששמים הוא רזא דאבהן, והיינו שזה מורה שעוד לא נתרחקו המדות ממקורם, שמכיר האדם שאין שום התנגדות בין המדות אלא שדבוקים במקורם, אבל אם כ"כ נתרחקו שכבר יש מקומות שנדמה לאדם שזה המקום אין ביכולתו להחזירו לאור ד', ואז נדמה להאדם שהמדות המה באמת הופכיים ויש התנגדות ביניהם, ואז נקרא מחלוקת שלא לשם שמים.
records.targetEnglish: As long as a person recognizes that God established these attributes for the person’s benefit, so that there would be a place for human service, and recognizes that no place in him is so distant from God’s light that he cannot return it to God, it is still called disagreement for the sake of Heaven. This is the Zohar’s saying that heaven is the mystery of the patriarchs: the attributes have not yet become distant from their source. The person recognizes no opposition between the attributes, since they are attached to their source. But when they have become so distant that a person thinks there are places he cannot return to God’s light, he then imagines the attributes to be truly opposite and in conflict with one another. This is called disagreement that is not for the sake of Heaven.
records.explanation: Tiferet supplies a concrete test for the common-root insight: differences remain ordered toward service and return, rather than being treated as independent, irreconcilable powers. The full Korach argument also rejects using primordial unity to abandon commandments. This preserves the origin’s hope of heart-level unity without dissolving the obligation to work through actual differences.

records.themeTitle: A threatened covenant can be rediscovered after failure
records.themeSummary: The opening distinction asks how Chanukah can disclose deliverance when the persecution had already produced religious failure.
records.originHebrew: עִנְיַן נֵס חֲנֻכָּה שֶׁאֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה לְנֵס פּוּרִים וּשְׁאָר גְּאֻלּוֹת: דְּשָׁם בִּקֵּשׁ הָמָן לְהַשְׁמִיד כָּל הַיְּהוּדִים, וְהָיָה הַנֵּס שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַיְּמָה מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ וְ"נַהֲפוֹךְ הוּא"; מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּימֵי הַיְּוָנִים שֶׁעָמְדוּ לְבַטֵּל אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת, וּכְפִי הָרְאוּת עָלְתָה בְּיָדָם אָז לְפִי שָׁעָה, שֶׁהַרְבֵּה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הֵמִירוּ דָּת רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלַן.
records.originEnglish: The miracle of Chanukah differs from the miracle of Purim and other deliverances. There Haman sought to destroy all the Jews, and the miracle was that his intention was not fulfilled: ‘It was turned about.’ This was not so in the Greeks’ days, when they arose to abolish Torah and commandments among Israel. To outward appearance they initially succeeded for a time, for many in Israel abandoned their faith, Heaven preserve us.
records.targetHebrew: אשר יש לאדם לפעמים פעולות כאלה אשר אינו רואה הכבוד שמים מאלו הפעולות, עד היכן שנדמה לו שבאותן הפעולות עשה ההיפך לגמרי ח"ו מרצון השי"ת. ואח"כ כשאדם עושה תשובה מאהבה, ומתפלל וצועק מעומק לבו להשי"ת, אז מאיר לו השי"ת שמעולם לא נעתק ח"ו מרצון השי"ת אפילו כחוט השערה.
records.targetEnglish: A person sometimes performs actions in which he sees no honor of Heaven, to the point that it seems to him that through those actions he did the complete opposite, Heaven forbid, of God’s will. Afterwards, when a person repents out of love, prays, and cries to God from the depth of his heart, God then illuminates for him that he was never uprooted, Heaven forbid, from God’s will, even by a hair’s breadth.
records.explanation: The full Tiferet passage opens with the promise of not rejecting Israel in the Greek period, then explains how repentance discloses an attachment hidden during apparent estrangement. This answers the kind of deliverance posed by the opening question; Rav Tzadok develops it through the repentant betrayers in the following paragraphs. Tiferet also applies the principle to Purim, but the comparison does not erase Rav Tzadok’s distinction between the two persecutions or claim that the failures never occurred.

records.themeTitle: Repentance awakens another through a real bond
records.themeSummary: The sudden response to Yosi ben Yoezer’s words is explained through the speaker’s bond with the other soul and the seriousness of his own self-offering.
records.originHebrew: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִכְנְסוּ בְּלִבּוֹ דִּבְרֵי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר וְקִיֵּם בְּעַצְמוֹ אַרְבַּע מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין וּבְשָׁעָה קַלָּה קְדָמוּהוּ לְיוֹסֵי לְגַן עֵדֶן. וְכֵן יוֹסֵף מְשִׁיתָא, אַף שֶׁפָּקַר מִקּוֹדֶם וְנִכְנַס לַהֵיכָל, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אַחַר כָּךְ לֹא נִתְרַצָּה, בִּמְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ, וְקִדֵּשׁ שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם. וְזֶהוּ "רֵיחַ בְּגָדָיו" דְּדָרַשׁ כְּמוֹ "רֵיחַ בּוֹגְדָיו" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סַנְהֶדְרִין ל״ז עַמּוּד א׳), וְהוּא שֶׁמֵּהָרֵיחַ שֶׁל הַבְּגִידָה שֶׁמִּקּוֹדֶם נִתְעַלָּה בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת, שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה פְּנִימִיּוּת לְבָבָם שֶׁבְּשֹׁרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקֻשָּׁרִים בְּהַקְּדֻשָּׁה, כְּעִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת י״ז עַמּוּד א׳): "גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לְפָנֶיךָ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנְךָ, וּמִי מְעַכֵּב שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִסָּה", וְזֶהוּ אַף בְּקַל שֶׁבַּקַּלִּים כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ הֵם מִקּוֹדֶם.
records.originEnglish: Nevertheless, Yosi ben Yoezer’s words entered his heart, and he carried out upon himself the four court-imposed deaths; within a short time he preceded Yosi to the Garden of Eden. So too Yosef Meshita: although he had previously rebelled and entered the Sanctuary, afterwards he would not consent to enter again, even at the cost of his life, and sanctified the divine Name. This is ‘the fragrance of his garments,’ expounded as ‘the fragrance of his betrayers,’ as in Sanhedrin 37a. From the fragrance of his previous betrayal he was elevated with still greater force, for the inner heart was revealed: at Israel’s root they are bound to holiness. This is the meaning of ‘It is revealed and known before You that our will is to do Your will; what prevents us is the leaven in the dough.’ This applies even to the most disreputable person, as they had been beforehand.
records.targetHebrew: וּשְׁאָר יְחִידִים שֶׁשָּׁבִים יֵשׁ לָהֶם יְכוֹלֶת לְהָשִׁיב רַק הַנְּפָשׁוֹת הַתְּלוּיִים בָּהֶם וּבְאוֹתוֹ כֹּחַ שֶׁשָּׁבִים], כְּאוֹתוֹ תַלְמִיד בִּמְנָחוֹת (מד.) שֶׁעַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ עוֹרֵר גַּם כֵּן הִרְהוּר תְּשׁוּבָה בְּאוֹתָהּ אִשָּׁה שֶׁהָיְתָה שַׁיָּיכֶת לוֹ, שֶׁהֲרֵי נַעֲשֵׂית אַחַר כָּךְ אִשְׁתּוֹ. וּמִי שֶׁמְּחוּיָּב מִיתָה בַּחֲטָאָיו, אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְעוֹרְרוֹ בִּתְשׁוּבָה עַד שֶׁיִּמְסוֹר נַפְשׁוֹ לְמִיתָה גַּם כֵּן, שֶׁזֶּהוּ מַדְרֵגַת תְּשׁוּבָתוֹ, וְאָז יוּכַל לְעוֹרֵר בּוֹ תְּשׁוּבָה. וּלְכָךְ פִּינְחָס עָצַר הַמַּגֵּפָה שֶׁהוּא עוֹנֶשׁ הַמַּגִּיעַ לִזְנוּת – אַנְדְּרָלָמוּסְיָא, רַק שֶׁשָּׁבוּ] עַל יְדֵי מְסִירַת נַפְשׁוֹ לְמִיתָה, וְעוֹרְרָם שֶׁשָּׁבוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב גַּבֵּי מִלְחֶמֶת מִדְיָן. וְכֵן בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה סה) בְּעוּבָדָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה, שֶׁרַק כְּשֶׁהוֹלִיכוּהוּ לַצְּלָב, אָז עוֹרֵר בִּתְשׁוּבָה לְבֶן אֲחוֹתוֹ. וְכֵן מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן נָפְלוּ עַל פְּנֵיהֶם בְּעֵת מַחֲלוֹקֶת קֹרַח, שֶׁרָאוּ שֶׁנִּגְזַר עֲלֵיהֶם מִיתָה וּמָסְרוּ נַפְשָׁם לְמִיתָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר, וּכְדֵי לְהַעֲלוֹתָם בִּתְשׁוּבָה; וְלֹא הוֹעִיל, לְפִי שֶׁהֵם נֶחְלְקוּ עָלָיו וְהִפְרִידוּ עַצְמָם מֵחִבּוּרָם בְּנַפְשׁוֹ, וּלְכָךְ לֹא פָּעַל הִתְעוֹרְרוּתוֹ בְּלִבָּם, כִּי בְּמִדָּה שֶׁאָדָם מוֹדֵד מוֹדְדִין לוֹ, וּבְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁרוֹצֶה לֵילֵךְ מוֹלִיכִין אוֹתוֹ:
records.targetEnglish: Other individuals who repent can bring back only the souls dependent upon them, and in the particular power in which they themselves return. Thus the student in Menachot 44a, through his repentance, awakened a thought of repentance in that woman who was related to him, for afterwards she became his wife. Someone liable to death through his sins cannot be awakened to repentance until the person awakening him also gives himself over even to death, for this is the level of that repentance; then he can awaken him to repentance. Therefore Pinchas stopped the plague, the indiscriminate calamity that is the punishment resulting from sexual immorality: they repented through his willingness to give his life, and he awakened them to return, as written concerning the war with Midian. So too in the account of Rabbi Yosi ben Yoezer of Tzeredah in Bereshit Rabbah: only when he was being led to the cross did he awaken his sister’s son to repentance. Likewise Moses and Aaron fell on their faces during Korach’s dispute, seeing that death had been decreed against them; they gave themselves over to death, as written in the Zohar, to raise them to repentance. But it did not help, because those people disputed him and separated themselves from their connection within his soul. His awakening therefore did not work in their hearts: a person is measured with the measure he uses, and is led along the path he wishes to follow.
records.explanation: Tzidkat interprets the same Yosi episode, rather than merely offering another story of a quick return. The explanation is relational: his words work at the moment his own life is at stake, within a bond that can transmit an awakening. The concluding Korach counterexample is retained, so the quotation does not imply that any righteous person’s suffering automatically causes someone else to repent. This is the author’s interpretation of the narrated events, not practical instruction to seek danger.

records.themeTitle: A moment of concealment does not define the inner will
records.themeSummary: The inner desire for divine service can be revealed beneath a failure, while reliance on the ancestral covenant never replaces service as a standing rule.
records.originHebrew: וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם נִכְנְסוּ בְּלִבּוֹ דִּבְרֵי יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר וְקִיֵּם בְּעַצְמוֹ אַרְבַּע מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין וּבְשָׁעָה קַלָּה קְדָמוּהוּ לְיוֹסֵי לְגַן עֵדֶן. וְכֵן יוֹסֵף מְשִׁיתָא, אַף שֶׁפָּקַר מִקּוֹדֶם וְנִכְנַס לַהֵיכָל, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אַחַר כָּךְ לֹא נִתְרַצָּה, בִּמְסִירַת נֶפֶשׁ, וְקִדֵּשׁ שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם. וְזֶהוּ "רֵיחַ בְּגָדָיו" דְּדָרַשׁ כְּמוֹ "רֵיחַ בּוֹגְדָיו" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סַנְהֶדְרִין ל״ז עַמּוּד א׳), וְהוּא שֶׁמֵּהָרֵיחַ שֶׁל הַבְּגִידָה שֶׁמִּקּוֹדֶם נִתְעַלָּה בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת, שֶׁנִּתְגַּלָּה פְּנִימִיּוּת לְבָבָם שֶׁבְּשֹׁרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקֻשָּׁרִים בְּהַקְּדֻשָּׁה, כְּעִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת י״ז עַמּוּד א׳): "גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לְפָנֶיךָ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנְךָ, וּמִי מְעַכֵּב שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִסָּה", וְזֶהוּ אַף בְּקַל שֶׁבַּקַּלִּים כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ הֵם מִקּוֹדֶם.
records.originEnglish: Nevertheless, Yosi ben Yoezer’s words entered his heart, and he carried out upon himself the four court-imposed deaths; within a short time he preceded Yosi to the Garden of Eden. So too Yosef Meshita: although he had previously rebelled and entered the Sanctuary, afterwards he would not consent to enter again, even at the cost of his life, and sanctified the divine Name. This is ‘the fragrance of his garments,’ expounded as ‘the fragrance of his betrayers,’ as in Sanhedrin 37a. From the fragrance of his previous betrayal he was elevated with still greater force, for the inner heart was revealed: at Israel’s root they are bound to holiness. This is the meaning of ‘It is revealed and known before You that our will is to do Your will; what prevents us is the leaven in the dough.’ This applies even to the most disreputable person, as they had been beforehand.
records.targetHebrew: וזרח משעיר למו הופיע מהר פארן וגו' והיינו, כי השי"ת נתן זריחה והופעה מאלו הכחות לישראל ג"כ. כי באמת יכול להיות אפילו אצל ישראל ג"כ, שיכול לשכוח ח"ו מעט בהשי"ת. ועל זה נתן השי"ת זריחה והופעה, כי מאחר שבמקום שישראל עומדים בדעה שלימה, שם הולכים בעבודה מצידם ואין סומכין עצמם על שום תקיפות. רק שלפעמים נסתר מהם, על זה מברר להם השי"ת, כי העומק לב של ישראל הוא מלא רצון ועבודה. ועל זה הרגע יוכלו לסמוך עצמם על התקיפות של קדושת אבות, כי השי"ת יבררם לטוב.
records.targetEnglish: ‘He shone from Seir for them; He appeared from Mount Paran.’ God also gave Israel a radiance and appearance from these powers. For in truth, even within Israel it can happen that a person forgets God a little, Heaven forbid. For this God gave a radiance and appearance: when Israel stands with complete understanding, they undertake service themselves and do not rely upon any source of strength. Only sometimes this is concealed from them. Concerning that, God clarifies for them that Israel’s deep heart is full of desire and service. For that moment they may rely upon the strength of the patriarchs’ holiness, for God will clarify them for good.
records.explanation: Tiferet supplies the qualification that makes the discovery of an enduring root intelligible: the normal posture is active service, and the lapse is a concealment of a deeper will. Its opening explicitly rejects treating the ancestral covenant as a reason to cease working. This illuminates Rav Tzadok’s claim that even a betrayer’s return reveals an inward will for holiness, without turning inherited holiness into advance permission to rebel.

records.themeTitle: Recognizing providence begins with the good one has received
records.themeSummary: Confidence after failure follows recognition of God’s help in good action; the ultimate disclosure of providence belongs to the completion of repentance.
records.originHebrew: אָמְנָם כִּי כֵּן הוּא הַסֵּדֶר: כְּשֶׁנִּתְוַדַּע לְאָדָם מִקּוֹדֶם בֶּטַח בְּנַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁמַּעֲשָׂיו הַטּוֹבִים אֵינָם מִכֹּחוֹ רַק מֵהַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְזֶהוּ "כְּשֶׁרָצִיתָ נָתַתָּ בְּלִבָּם לֶאֱהֹב" אָז גַּם אִם חָלִילָה יִזְדַּמֵּן לְפָנָיו לִפְעָמִים אֵיזֶה מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁלֹּא כַּהֹגֶן, יוּכַל לִבְטֹחַ שֶׁגַּם זֶה הָיָה בְּהַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהַיְנוּ "נָתַתָּ בְּלִבָּם לִשְׂנֹא". וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "הַשֵּׁם רֹעִי לֹא אֶחְסָר וְגוֹמֵר יַנְחֵנִי בְמַעְגְּלֵי צֶדֶק לְמַעַן שְׁמוֹ" הַיְנוּ שֶׁהָיָה בָּרוּר לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוֹעוֹ וּמַנְהִיגוֹ לָלֶכֶת בְּמַעְגְּלֵי צֶדֶק וְיֹשֶׁר וְלֹא בְּכֹחוֹ יִגְבַּר; עַל יְדֵי זֶה: "גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ וְגוֹמֵר" לִפְעָמִים, גַּם כֵּן "לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי", שֶׁגַּם שָׁם אַתָּה עִמָּדִי.
records.originEnglish: This is indeed the order. When a person first comes to know with certainty within himself that his good deeds do not come from his own power but from God’s providence—‘When You willed, You placed love in their hearts’—then, even if some improper deed should occasionally come his way, Heaven forbid, he can trust that this too was under God’s providence: ‘You placed hatred in their hearts.’ King David alludes to this: ‘The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not lack … He leads me in paths of righteousness for His name’s sake.’ It was clear before him that God shepherds and guides him in upright, righteous paths, and that he does not prevail through his own power. Through this, even when ‘I walk …’ at times, ‘I will fear no evil, for You are with me’: there too You are with me.
records.targetHebrew: כִּי זֶה יְסוֹד אֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית — לָתֵת מָקוֹם לַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא הַמֻּזְהֶרֶת בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת אָדָם, וּמֵאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ ע"ה הִתְחִיל ״שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה״ וּשְׁלֵימוּתָהּ עַל יְדֵי מָשִׁיחַ, שֶׁיְּתֻקַּן כָּל הַקּוֹדֵם — גַּם חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן — דְּיִתְהַפֵּךְ הַכֹּל לִזְכִיּוֹת; זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק עַל יְדֵי הִתְגַּלּוּת הַקֵּירוּב הַגָּמוּר מִמֶּנּוּ יִתְבָּרַךְ וַהֲסָרַת הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת לְגַמְרֵי, כִּי יִתְבָּרֵר דְּ״גַם כָּל מַחְשְׁבוֹתֵינוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂינוּ פָּעַלְתָּ לָנוּ״, וְהַכֹּל מִמֶּנּוּ יִתְבָּרֵךְ כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה [פד, יז] בַּאֲחֵי יוֹסֵף ״כְּשֶׁרָצִיתָ נָתַתָּ בְּלִבָּם לֶאֱהֹב, וּכְשֶׁרָצִיתָ״ כו’, וְכָךְ רָצָה יִתְבָּרֵךְ לָתֵת בְּלֵב הָאָדָם לִשְׂנֹא — וְגַם זֶה מֵאִתּוֹ יִתְבָּרֵךְ שֶׁרָצָה לְקָרְבוֹ עַל דֶּרֶךְ זֶה, וְהָרִיחוּקִים הַכֹּל הֵם קֵירוּבִים, כְּעִנְיַן ״יִסּוּרִים שֶׁל אַהֲבָה״ שֶׁהֲרֵי הַיִּסּוּר הוּא רִיחוּק וְהֵיפֶךְ הָאַהֲבָה, וּבִשְׁעַת מַעֲשֶׂה כִּסְבוּרִים אָנוּ שֶׁהוּא רִיחוּק, וּבֶאֱמֶת אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא קֵירוּב וְתֹקֶף אַהֲבָה; וְכֵן כָּל הָעֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁהֵבִיאוּ הָאָדָם לָשׁוּב וְלִזְכּוֹת לְמַדְרֵיגַת בַּעַל תְּשׁוּבָה — הֲרֵי הָרִיחוּק הוּא סִבַּת קֵירוּב
records.targetEnglish: This is the foundation of the Israelite people: to give place to Torah, which commands human effort. With Abraham began the ‘two thousand years of Torah.’ Its completion comes through Messiah, who will repair everything preceding, including Adam’s sin, so that everything is transformed into merits. This is possible only through the disclosure of complete nearness from God and the complete removal of effort, for it will be clarified that ‘all our thoughts and actions You have accomplished for us,’ and that everything is from Him. Thus Bereshit Rabbah says of Joseph’s brothers, ‘When You willed, You placed love in their hearts, and when You willed …’. God likewise willed to place hatred within the human heart. This too came from Him, who wished to bring the person near by this path. All the distances are approaches, like ‘sufferings of love’: suffering is distance and the opposite of love, and at the time we think it is distance; in truth it is nearness and intense love. So too all the transgressions that brought a person to return and attain the level of a penitent: the distance was the cause of nearness.
records.explanation: Takanat expounds the same paired love-and-hatred saying within the movement from Abraham’s tested effort to Messiah’s completed repair. Its opening expressly preserves Torah’s demand for effort, and its retrospective claim concerns failures that actually brought a person to return. This locates Rav Tzadok’s confidence within an ordered process; it is not a claim that effort or repentance can be bypassed now.

records.themeTitle: Being shepherded means continually seeking the divine will
records.themeSummary: The shepherd image attributes good action to God while requiring the person to keep looking and praying for guidance in each concrete act.
records.originHebrew: אָמְנָם כִּי כֵּן הוּא הַסֵּדֶר: כְּשֶׁנִּתְוַדַּע לְאָדָם מִקּוֹדֶם בֶּטַח בְּנַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁמַּעֲשָׂיו הַטּוֹבִים אֵינָם מִכֹּחוֹ רַק מֵהַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְזֶהוּ "כְּשֶׁרָצִיתָ נָתַתָּ בְּלִבָּם לֶאֱהֹב" אָז גַּם אִם חָלִילָה יִזְדַּמֵּן לְפָנָיו לִפְעָמִים אֵיזֶה מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁלֹּא כַּהֹגֶן, יוּכַל לִבְטֹחַ שֶׁגַּם זֶה הָיָה בְּהַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהַיְנוּ "נָתַתָּ בְּלִבָּם לִשְׂנֹא". וְעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: "הַשֵּׁם רֹעִי לֹא אֶחְסָר וְגוֹמֵר יַנְחֵנִי בְמַעְגְּלֵי צֶדֶק לְמַעַן שְׁמוֹ" הַיְנוּ שֶׁהָיָה בָּרוּר לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוֹעוֹ וּמַנְהִיגוֹ לָלֶכֶת בְּמַעְגְּלֵי צֶדֶק וְיֹשֶׁר וְלֹא בְּכֹחוֹ יִגְבַּר; עַל יְדֵי זֶה: "גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ וְגוֹמֵר" לִפְעָמִים, גַּם כֵּן "לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי", שֶׁגַּם שָׁם אַתָּה עִמָּדִי.
records.originEnglish: This is indeed the order. When a person first comes to know with certainty within himself that his good deeds do not come from his own power but from God’s providence—‘When You willed, You placed love in their hearts’—then, even if some improper deed should occasionally come his way, Heaven forbid, he can trust that this too was under God’s providence: ‘You placed hatred in their hearts.’ King David alludes to this: ‘The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not lack … He leads me in paths of righteousness for His name’s sake.’ It was clear before him that God shepherds and guides him in upright, righteous paths, and that he does not prevail through his own power. Through this, even when ‘I walk …’ at times, ‘I will fear no evil, for You are with me’: there too You are with me.
records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayechi 3
records.targetHebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר הָאֱלֹקִים אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלְּכוּ אֲבוֹתַי לְפָנָיו הָאֱלֹקִים הָרוֹעֶה אוֹתִי מֵעוֹדִי. הַיְינוּ שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ הָיָה מַקְטִין עַצְמוֹ נֶגֶד אֲבוֹתָיו אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק, וְאָמַר כִּי לָהֶם הָיָה חָכְמָה וּבִינָה גְּדוֹלָה מְאֹד עַד כִּי הִרְחִיבוּ אֶת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵעַצְמָם, וְאַף אִם פָּתַח לָהֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ פֶּתַח קָטָן, הָיוּ מַרְחִיבִים וּמִתְפַּשְּׁטִים אוֹתוֹ בְּחָכְמָתָם כְּדֵי לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן בּוֹרְאָם, וְהֵבִינוּ אַף בְּדָבָר שֶׁלֹּא הֵאִיר לָהֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְפֹרָשׁ, וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ "אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלְּכוּ" הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיוּ הוֹלְכִים בְּכֹחָם. אֲבָל אֲנִי, "הָאֱלֹקִים הָרוֹעֶה אוֹתִי מֵעוֹדִי עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה", הַיְינוּ בְּכָל פְּרָט מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁאֲנִי עוֹשֶׂה, אֲנִי צָרִיךְ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָאִיר עֵינַי אֵיךְ הוּא רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְאַף בְּזֶה הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁרָאִיתִי אֵיךְ הוּא רְצוֹנוֹ, אִם רְצוֹנוֹ לְשַׁנּוֹתָהּ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם צָרִיךְ אֲנִי לִרְאוֹת גַּם בַּפַּעַם הַשֵּׁנִית אֵיךְ הוּא רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּבֶאֱמֶת בְּזֶה הָעִנְיָן הָיָה יַעֲקֹב הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבָּאָבוֹת כִּי זֹאת הִיא מַדְרֵגָה גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַנְהִיג אֶת הָאָדָם תָּמִיד, וְזֹאת הָיְתָה תְּפִלַּת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (תְּהִלִּים כָּף גִּימֶל, אָלֶף) "הַשֵּׁם רוֹעִי לֹא אֶחְסָר", הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא אַחְסִיר הַשְׁגָּחַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עָלַי וְרַק שֶׁיִּהְיֶה רוֹעֶה אוֹתִי תָּמִיד וְגַם אֲנִי אַכִּיר תָּמִיד שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא רוֹעִי, כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּטוּבוֹ מַנְהִיג כָּל דָּבָר, אַךְ שֶׁהָאָדָם מַחְזִיר פָּנָיו וְאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לְצַפּוֹת וּלְהִתְפַּלֵּל, וּבְעֵת שֶׁהָאָדָם יִתְפַּלֵּל תְּפִלָּה שְׁלֵימָה אָז תֵּיכֶף יֵעָנֶה, וְיִרְאֶה כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הָרוֹעֶה וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ "לֹא אֶחְסָר" הַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא אַחְזִיר פָּנַי מִמֶּנּוּ.
records.targetEnglish: ‘He said: the God before whom my fathers walked, the God who has shepherded me from my earliest days.’ Jacob was making himself small before his fathers Abraham and Isaac. He said that they possessed very great wisdom and understanding, so that they expanded God’s will through their own powers. Even when God opened a small opening for them, they expanded and extended it through their wisdom to do their Creator’s will, understanding even a matter God had not explicitly illuminated for them. This is ‘before whom they walked’: they walked through their own strength. But I—‘the God who has shepherded me from my earliest days until this day’—in every particular action I perform, I need God to illuminate my eyes as to His will. Even in an action in which I have already seen His will, if it is to be repeated, I still need to see on the second occasion what His will is. In truth, in this respect Jacob was the greatest of the patriarchs, for it is a great level that God should guide a person continually. This was King David’s prayer: ‘The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not lack.’ That is, I should not lack God’s providence over me; He should always shepherd me, and I too should always recognize that God is my shepherd. In His goodness God guides everything, but the person turns his face away and does not wish to look expectantly and pray. When a person prays a complete prayer, he is immediately answered and sees that God is the shepherd. This is ‘I shall not lack’: I shall not turn my face away from Him.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach interprets the same psalm phrase as continual recognition, rather than personal control over providence. Its account of Jacob explains why attributing even good deeds to God does not make the person passive: a repeated act still calls for renewed attention to God’s will. This develops the positive premise on which Rav Tzadok builds his confidence after failure.

Clarified antecedents and grammatical referents are integrated into the English; original authorial asides remain explicit; the relation explanation is editorial and is not part of the quotation.

records.themeTitle: Completed return changes the divine assessment of the past
records.themeSummary: The reversal of deliberate sins into merits is described from the standpoint of completed repentance and divine disclosure, with an explicit limit on ordinary human judgment.
records.originHebrew: אָמְנָם דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא "הַגֶּבֶר הֻקַם עָל", שֶׁהֵקִים עֻלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, הַיְנוּ שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִתָּקֵן גַּם הַפְּגָם שֶׁמִּקּוֹדֶם שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נַעֲשׂוֹת כִּזְכֻיּוֹת; וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּתְבָּרֵר שֶׁגַּם זֶה הָיָה מֵהַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ מִקּוֹדֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שַׁבָּת פ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): "אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית", וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּתְוַדַּע שֶׁכֵּן הָיָה מְסֻדָּר לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהוּא בְּחִינַת "לְאַהֲפָכָא חֲשׁוֹכָא לִנְהוֹרָא". וְזֶה שֹׁרֶשׁ אוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד שֶׁהֵמָּה חַיֵּי עוֹלָם, שֶׁיִּתְבָּרְרוּ שֶׁכָּל הַקִּלְקוּלִים הָיָה מֵהַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְיִתֻּקְּנוּ בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת לִהְיוֹת "טוֹב מְאֹד", יוֹתֵר מִצַּדִּיק מֵעִקָּרוֹ, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ קִיּוּם. וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת ל״ד עַמּוּד ב׳): "מָקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין, צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים אֵינָם עוֹמְדִין".
records.originEnglish: King David, however, is ‘the man raised on high,’ who established the yoke of repentance: even the prior damage can be repaired so that the transgressions become merits. It will be clarified that this too was under God’s providence beforehand, as in ‘If your sins are like years’—like these years ordered and coming from the six days of Creation. It will become known that this was arranged before Him. This is turning darkness into light. This is the root of the light of Messiah son of David, which is eternal life: it will be clarified that all the damages were under God’s providence, and they will be repaired with greater force to become ‘very good,’ beyond someone righteous from the outset. The latter is the aspect of Messiah son of Joseph, who will not endure. This is ‘In the place where penitents stand, the completely righteous do not stand.’
records.targetHebrew: וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַחֲסִידֶיךָ יְרַנֵּנוּ", וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי יְשַׁעְיָה רֶמֶז רצו): אֵלּוּ רִשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּלֵי, וְכֵן עַל פָּסוּק "אִסְפוּ לִי חֲסִידָי וְגוֹמֵר" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם). פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי "חָסִיד" הוּא הַנּוֹטֶה מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין לְהִתְחַסֵּד, וְכֵן רָשָׁע נוֹטֶה מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין לְהַרְשִׁיעַ; וּכְשֶׁיִּפְתַּח הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לֶעָתִיד אַחַר הַתְּשׁוּבָה הַגְּמוּרָה, וְיַכִּירוּ הַכֹּל כֹּחַ מַלְכוּתוֹ, נִמְצָא הַזְּדוֹנוֹת שֶׁהָיוּ נְטִיָּה מִשּׁוּרַת הַדִּין – הָיוּ חֲסִידוּת, כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ נוֹטִים מֵאֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְדָיֵיק "חֲסִידָי" וַ"חֲסִידֶיךָ", וְלֹא "חֲסִידִים", רַק שֶׁאֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵם קְרוּיִים חֲסִידִים, וְלֹא לְעֵינֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם.
records.targetEnglish: This is ‘Your devoted ones will sing joyfully’; the Sages say that these are the wicked of Israel, and likewise concerning ‘Gather to Me My devoted ones.’ A devoted person is one who departs from the line of strict law in order to act with extra devotion, while a wicked person departs from that line in order to do evil. When God opens this understanding in the future, after complete repentance, and everyone recognizes the power of His kingship, the deliberate sins that were a departure from the line of law turn out to have been devotion, since they did not depart from the truth of God’s will. The text precisely says ‘My devoted ones’ and ‘Your devoted ones,’ not simply ‘devoted ones’: they are called devoted before God, not in human eyes.
records.explanation: Tzidkat clarifies whose assessment is being described and when: the disclosure follows complete repentance, and the text deliberately says “My” or “Your” devoted ones. This makes Rav Tzadok’s dramatic retrospective claim more precise. It does not license people to relabel a current transgression as a meritorious deed.
