records.themeTitle: The height reached through repentance does not make sin the preferred path
records.themeSummary: A penitent may recover holiness from a deeper place, while God’s primary desire remains upright righteousness.
records.originHebrew: אָמְנָם דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא "הַגֶּבֶר הֻקַם עָל", שֶׁהֵקִים עֻלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה, הַיְנוּ שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִתָּקֵן גַּם הַפְּגָם שֶׁמִּקּוֹדֶם שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נַעֲשׂוֹת כִּזְכֻיּוֹת; וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּתְבָּרֵר שֶׁגַּם זֶה הָיָה מֵהַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ מִקּוֹדֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (שַׁבָּת פ״ט עַמּוּד ב׳): "אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית", וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּתְוַדַּע שֶׁכֵּן הָיָה מְסֻדָּר לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהוּא בְּחִינַת "לְאַהֲפָכָא חֲשׁוֹכָא לִנְהוֹרָא". וְזֶה שֹׁרֶשׁ אוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד שֶׁהֵמָּה חַיֵּי עוֹלָם, שֶׁיִּתְבָּרְרוּ שֶׁכָּל הַקִּלְקוּלִים הָיָה מֵהַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְיִתֻּקְּנוּ בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת לִהְיוֹת "טוֹב מְאֹד", יוֹתֵר מִצַּדִּיק מֵעִקָּרוֹ, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ קִיּוּם. וְזֶה מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת ל״ד עַמּוּד ב׳): "מָקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְּשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין, צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים אֵינָם עוֹמְדִין".
records.originEnglish: King David, however, is ‘the man raised on high,’ who established the yoke of repentance: even the prior damage can be repaired so that the transgressions become merits. It will be clarified that this too was under God’s providence beforehand, as in ‘If your sins are like years’—like these years ordered and coming from the six days of Creation. It will become known that this was arranged before Him. This is turning darkness into light. This is the root of the light of Messiah son of David, which is eternal life: it will be clarified that all the damages were under God’s providence, and they will be repaired with greater force to become ‘very good,’ beyond someone righteous from the outset. The latter is the aspect of Messiah son of Joseph, who will not endure. This is ‘In the place where penitents stand, the completely righteous do not stand.’
records.targetHebrew: וְנִרְאֶה דְּעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ב׳:ה׳): ״׳חֹשֶׁךְ׳ — זֶה מַעֲשֵׂיהֶן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים... אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ בְּמִי חָפֵץ יוֹתֵר וְכוּלֵיהּ״ וְאֵיךְ סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ שֶׁיַּחְפּוֹץ בְּמַעֲשֵׂה רְשָׁעִים?! רַק הַכַּוָּונָה כְּפִי הַבְּרִיאָה, דְּ״עָשָׂה הָאֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָדָם יָשָׁר״ (קֹהֶלֶת ז:כט) וְאַף דְּבָרָא רְשָׁעִים וְיֵצֶר הָרָע, בָּרָא תּוֹרָה תַּבְלִין (קִדּוּשִׁין ל׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) לִהְיוֹת: ״נֵר לְרַגְלִי [דְבָרֶךָ, וְאוֹר לִנְתִיבָתִי]״ (תְּהִלִּים קי״ט:ק״ה) דְּ״גַּם כִּי אֵשֵׁב בַּחֹשֶׁךְ — ה׳ אוֹר לִי״ (מִיכָה ז:ח), וְ״גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ בְּגֵיא [צַלְמָוֶת לֹא אִירָא רָע, כִּי] אַתָּה עִמָּדִי״ (תְּהִלִּים כ״ג:ד׳) וְאַף דְּסוֹף דִּקְרִיבִין יַתִּיר, כִּי הוּא מַעֲלֶה נִיצוֹצוֹת קְדוֹשִׁים מִמְּקוֹמוֹת חַיּוּתוֹ שְׁפֵלִים, וּמְהַפֵּךְ חֲשׁוֹכָא לִנְהוֹרָא וְסָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָפֵץ זֶה יוֹתֵר עַל זֶה אָמְרוּ: ״וַיַּרְא [אֱלֹהִים אֶת] הָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית א:ד), דְּמִכָּל מָקוֹם עִיקַּר חֶפְצוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּצַּדִּיק ״כִּי טוֹב״
records.targetEnglish: It seems that this is what Bereshit Rabbah means: “‘Darkness’—these are the deeds of the wicked … I do not know which He desires more.” How could one suppose that He desires the deeds of the wicked?! The intention concerns the created order: ‘God made the human being upright.’ Although He created wicked people and the evil inclination, He created Torah as its seasoning, to be ‘a lamp for my feet’—‘even when I sit in darkness, the Lord is my light,’ and ‘even when I walk in the valley … You are with me.’ Although in the end the penitent is nearer, because he raises holy sparks from the lowly places in which his vitality had been and turns darkness into light, so that one might suppose God desires this more, it is concerning this that they said, ‘God saw the light, that it was good.’ Nevertheless His essential desire and will is for the righteous person, ‘for it was good.’
records.explanation: Yisrael Kedoshim asks the ethical question raised by the origin’s comparison: does greater closeness after return mean that sin is preferred? Its answer keeps both claims: repentance raises sparks from a low place, yet God desires the upright path. This directly limits a possible misreading of “more than someone righteous from the outset.” The full canonical paragraph was read; the selected excerpt stays clear of its embedded later section headings.
records.translationProvenance: English quotations translated or checked anew against the exact canonical Hebrew during the Chanukah review. Clarified antecedents and grammatical referents are integrated into the English; original authorial asides remain explicit; the relation explanation is editorial and is not part of the quotation.

records.themeTitle: Judah finds renewed courage after failure
records.themeSummary: The Davidic line’s greater deliverance is expressed as courage awakened after a fall and as a further clarification still to be completed.

records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayechi 5
records.targetHebrew: וּבְדַם עֲנָבִים סוּתֹה. סוּתֹה הַיְינוּ לְשׁוֹן הֲסָתָה כִּי הַהֲסָתָה שֶׁל שׁוֹרֶשׁ יְהוּדָא הִיא אַחֲרֵי הַחֵטְא וּמִכְשׁוֹל שֶׁאֵירַע לוֹ יִתְעוֹרֵר עוֹז בְּנַפְשׁוֹ, אֵין זֹאת רַק שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִרְצֶה לְהוֹשִׁיעֵנִי בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת, כִּי עֲנָבִים הַיְינוּ טָעוּת וְשִׁכְחָה, וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ אָמַר (דְּבָרִים לָמֶד בֵּית, יוֹד דָּלֶת) "וְדַם עֵנָב תִּשְׁתֶּה חָמֶר", חָמֶר מוֹרֶה עַל "עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה אֱלֹקִים זוּלָתְךָ" כִּי אֵין מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת מַכִּירִין בִּלְשׁוֹן אֲרָמִי (שַׁבָּת יוֹד בֵּית עַמּוּד בֵּית). רַק מֹשֶׁה מִלְּגָאו וְיַעֲקֹב מִלְּבַר, כִּי אֵצֶל יַעֲקֹב נֶאֱמַר עֲנָבִים הַיְינוּ שְׁנֵי טָעוּתִים יְבָרֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל שֵׁבֶט יְהוּדָא הַיְינוּ יִצְרָא דַּעֲרָיוֹת וְיִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וּבֵירֵר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא נָקִי בִּשְׁתֵּיהֶן, וּמֹשֶׁה מִלְּגָאו כִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם רָאָה כִּי אֵין לִיהוּדָא שׁוּם טָעוּת בְּיִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כִּי בָּזֶה כְּבָר נִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁהוּא נָקִי מְאֹד, רַק יִצְרָא דַּעֲרָיוֹת צָרִיךְ עוֹד לְהִתְבָּרֵר, כִּדְאָמַר רַב (סַנְהֶדְרִין סָמֶךְ גִּימֶל עַמּוּד בֵּית) "לֹא עָבְדוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת הָעֵגֶל אֶלָּא לְהַתִּיר לָהֶם עֲרָיוֹת בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא" אֲבָל בְּיִצְרָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כְּבָר הֵם נְקִיִּים וְהָבֵן.
records.targetEnglish: ‘His garment in the blood of grapes.’ Sotoh is read as a term for an impulse, for the impulse at Judah’s root is this: after a sin or stumbling that has occurred to him, strength awakens in his soul—this can only mean that God wishes to save me with still greater force. Grapes signify error and forgetfulness. Moses said, ‘You drank the blood of the grape as wine.’ Chamer points to ‘no eye has seen, O God, besides You,’ for the ministering angels do not recognize Aramaic. But Moses is within, while Jacob is outside. In Jacob’s words it says ‘grapes’: God will clarify two errors concerning Judah’s tribe, the inclination toward sexual transgression and the inclination toward idolatry, and God clarified that he is clean in both. Moses is within, for Moses saw that Judah has no error in the inclination toward idolatry: in this he had already been clarified as very clean. Only the inclination toward sexual transgression still needs clarification, as Rav said, ‘Israel worshipped the calf only to permit themselves sexual transgression openly.’ But concerning the inclination toward idolatry they are already clean. Understand this.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach assigns Judah a specific response after stumbling: renewed confidence in a greater deliverance. Its distinction between Jacob’s outer expression and Moses’ inner view explains why a clarified root can coexist with further clarification still needed. The quotation does not assert that the calf’s act was permissible; its final rabbinic saying distinguishes the motive for that act. This illuminates the Davidic pattern in Rav Tzadok’s paragraph without making failure something to seek.

records.themeTitle: An unpurified heart can misuse inward illumination
records.themeSummary: The hidden light requires fear and purification because an impure heart can mistake what flows from itself for divine wisdom.
records.originHebrew: אָמְנָם אֵין הָעוֹלָם כְּדַאי לָזֶה, כִּי עַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכְלוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְהָקֵל בְּנַפְשָׁם לְלוֹמַר "לֵית דִּין וְלֵית דַּיָּן", וְיַעֲשֶׂה מַה שֶּׁלִּבּוֹ חָפֵץ; וְלָכֵן גְּנָזוֹ רַק לַצַּדִּיקִים לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא, כְּמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "מָה רַב טוּבְךָ אֲשֶׁר צָפַנְתָּ לִּירֵאֶיךָ" הַיְנוּ לַיָּרֵא וְחָרֵד בְּנַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ תָּמִיד, וְיוֹדֵעַ בְּנַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁמַּעֲשָׂיו אֵינָם כַּהֹגֶן, כִּי עַל יְדֵי יִרְאָה בָּא לִתְשׁוּבָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא יָשְׁרוּ מַעֲשָׂיו בְּעֵינָיו לְנֶגֶד גְּדֻלַּת הַבּוֹרֵא, אֵלָיו נִצְפַּן הֶאָרָה זוֹ: כִּי גַּם כָּל הַבְּגִידוֹת הֵמָּה בְּהַשְׁגָּחָה, וְנִתְקַן הַכֹּל לִהְיוֹת טוֹב כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
records.originEnglish: The world, however, is not worthy of this, for through it people could, Heaven forbid, become lenient with themselves, saying, ‘There is no judgment and no judge,’ and do whatever their heart desires. Therefore He concealed it only for the righteous in the future, as it says, ‘How abundant is Your goodness that You have stored up for those who fear You.’ This means the one who is fearful and trembling within, who feels that he never fully fulfills his obligation and knows within himself that his deeds are not proper. Through fear he comes to repentance, because his deeds do not seem right in his eyes before the Creator’s greatness. For him this illumination is stored: even all the betrayals are under providence, and everything is repaired to become good, as explained above.
records.targetHebrew: וְהָאוֹר הוּא הַחָכְמָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "תּוֹרָה אוֹר", וּכְשֶׁיּוֹצֵאת מִמְּקוֹם הַיִּרְאָה צוֹפָה מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ וְנִסְתַּכֵּל בָּרְשָׁעִים וּגְנָזוֹ, כִּי אֵין לְגַלּוֹתוֹ לָרְשָׁעִים כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, שֶׁמִּי שֶׁאֵין לִבּוֹ נָקִי כָּל כָּךְ, כַּאֲשֶׁר יַשִּׂיג הַחָכְמָה שֶׁנּוֹבֵעַ מִן הַלֵּב, יִהְיוּ נוֹבֵעַ מִלִּבּוֹ דִּבְרֵי דֹּפִי כְּדֹפִי לִבּוֹ לְפִי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַלֵּב דָּבוּק כִּתְאוֹמִים כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, שֶׁנּוֹבֵעַ רַק מַה שֶּׁהוּא רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
records.targetEnglish: The light is wisdom, as it says, ‘Torah is light.’ When it comes forth from the place of fear, it sees from one end of the world to the other. He looked upon the wicked and concealed it, because it must not be revealed to the wicked, as explained above. If someone whose heart is not sufficiently pure attains the wisdom that flows from the heart, tainted words will flow from his heart according to his heart’s own defects. The heart must be joined to God like twins, as explained above, so that only what is God’s will flows from it.
records.explanation: Dover gives a reason for the restriction on hidden light: inward fluency can carry the heart’s remaining defects. Its requirement of fear and purity illuminates why Rav Tzadok reserves the providential insight for someone moved toward repentance by fear, rather than for someone looking for permission to follow desire.

records.themeTitle: A desire’s claimed divine origin does not authorize it
records.themeSummary: Rav Tzadok’s warning against excusing wrongdoing is sharpened by a reading of Adam’s mistake: prior divine help does not make a compromised judgment reliable.
records.originHebrew: אָמְנָם אֵין הָעוֹלָם כְּדַאי לָזֶה, כִּי עַל יְדֵי זֶה יוּכְלוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לְהָקֵל בְּנַפְשָׁם לְלוֹמַר "לֵית דִּין וְלֵית דַּיָּן", וְיַעֲשֶׂה מַה שֶּׁלִּבּוֹ חָפֵץ; וְלָכֵן גְּנָזוֹ רַק לַצַּדִּיקִים לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא, כְּמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "מָה רַב טוּבְךָ אֲשֶׁר צָפַנְתָּ לִּירֵאֶיךָ" הַיְנוּ לַיָּרֵא וְחָרֵד בְּנַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ תָּמִיד, וְיוֹדֵעַ בְּנַפְשׁוֹ שֶׁמַּעֲשָׂיו אֵינָם כַּהֹגֶן, כִּי עַל יְדֵי יִרְאָה בָּא לִתְשׁוּבָה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא יָשְׁרוּ מַעֲשָׂיו בְּעֵינָיו לְנֶגֶד גְּדֻלַּת הַבּוֹרֵא, אֵלָיו נִצְפַּן הֶאָרָה זוֹ: כִּי גַּם כָּל הַבְּגִידוֹת הֵמָּה בְּהַשְׁגָּחָה, וְנִתְקַן הַכֹּל לִהְיוֹת טוֹב כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
records.originEnglish: The world, however, is not worthy of this, for through it people could, Heaven forbid, become lenient with themselves, saying, ‘There is no judgment and no judge,’ and do whatever their heart desires. Therefore He concealed it only for the righteous in the future, as it says, ‘How abundant is Your goodness that You have stored up for those who fear You.’ This means the one who is fearful and trembling within, who feels that he never fully fulfills his obligation and knows within himself that his deeds are not proper. Through fear he comes to repentance, because his deeds do not seem right in his eyes before the Creator’s greatness. For him this illumination is stored: even all the betrayals are under providence, and everything is repaired to become good, as explained above.
records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Bereshit 11
records.targetHebrew: וַיֹּאמֶר הָאָדָם הָאִשָּׁה אֲשֶׁר נָתַתָּ עִמָּדִי הִיא נָתְנָה וְכוּלֵי. כִּי בֶאֱמֶת טָעוּת אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּחֶטְאוֹ נִצְמַח מִזֶּה, כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָמַר "אֶעֱשֶׂה לּוֹ עֵזֶר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ" בְּיַעַן כִּי כַאֲשֶׁר נֶאֱסַר לְאָדָם לֶאֱכוֹל מֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת פָּחַד מְאֹד כִּי אָמַר בְּוַדַּאי לֹא אָסַר לִי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רַק מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בִּי חֶסְרוֹן, אַךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר בָּרָא לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֶת חַוָּה וְנִתְּנָה לוֹ לְעֵזֶר הַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּלֵךְ אַחַר דַּעְתָּהּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (בְּרֵאשִׁית כא, יב) "כֹּל אֲשֶׁר תֹּאמַר אֵלֶיךָ שָׂרָה שְׁמַע בְּקוֹלָהּ" וְאָז נִתְקָרֵר דַּעְתּוֹ, וְזֶה שֶׁטָּעַן הָאָדָם, "הָאִשָּׁה אֲשֶׁר נָתַתָּ עִמָּדִי", הַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה מֻתָּר לוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל עַל פִּי דִּבּוּרָהּ. אַךְ עִנְיַן חֶטְאוֹ הָיָה כְּמוֹ דְּאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא: תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁמּוֹרֶה הֲלָכָה וּבָא, אִם קוֹדֶם מַעֲשֶׂה אָמַר שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ וְאִם לְאַחַר מַעֲשֶׂה אֵין שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ (קִדּוּשִׁין עַמּוּד ע) וְהַיְינוּ מֵחֲמַת שֶׁהוּא נוֹגֵעַ בַּדָּבָר מֵאַחַר שֶׁכְּבָר עָשָׂה מַעֲשֶׂה, וְכֵן כָּאן אַף שֶׁהָיָה צָרִיךְ לִשְׁמֹעַ בְּקוֹלָהּ מִכָּל מָקוֹם מִכֵּיוָן שֶׁכְּבָר עָשְׂתָה מַעֲשֶׂיהָ לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לִשְׁמֹעַ אֵלֶיהָ בְּמָה שֶׁנָּתְנָה לוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל. וְטַעֲנָתָהּ הָיְתָה, "הַנָּחָשׁ הִשִּׁיאַנִי וָאוֹכֵל", שֶׁהֵבִיא הֲסָתָה וְחֶמְדָּה בְּלִבּוֹ וּסְבָרָתוֹ שֶׁהַחֵשֶׁק הִיא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּבֶאֱמֶת מֵאַחַר שֶׁאָדָם בְּעַצְמוֹ קָרָא אֶת שְׁמוֹ נָחָשׁ וְנָחָשׁ הַיְינוּ רַמַּאי כְּמוֹ מְנַחֵשׁ שֶׁהוּא מְרַמֶּה וְצָבוּעַ, הַיְינוּ שֶׁיוּכַל לְהַרְאוֹת לַחֲבֵרוֹ דָּבָר שֶׁיִּדְמֶה לוֹ כִּי מֵה' הוּא, עַל כֵּן הָיָה צָרִיךְ לִשְׁמוֹר אֶת עַצְמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִטְעֶה מֵאַחַר שֶׁיָּדַע שֶׁנִּמְצָא טָעוּת.
records.targetEnglish: ‘The human said: the woman whom You gave to be with me—she gave me …’. In truth, Adam’s mistake in his sin arose from God’s saying, ‘I shall make him a helper corresponding to him.’ When Adam was forbidden to eat from the tree of knowledge, he was very afraid: he said that God surely forbade it only because He knew there was a deficiency within him. But when God created Eve and gave her to him as a helper, meaning that he should follow her judgment—as Abraham was told, ‘Whatever Sarah tells you, listen to her voice’—his mind was reassured. This was Adam’s claim: ‘The woman whom You gave to be with me,’ meaning that he was permitted to eat according to her word. His sin, however, was as in the Talmud’s rule: a scholar who comes with a ruling is heeded if he stated it before the event, but is not heeded if he states it after the event. For after he has already acted, he has a personal interest in the matter. So here: although Adam needed to listen to her, once she had already acted he should not have listened when she gave him food to eat. Her claim was, ‘The serpent deceived me, and I ate.’ It brought enticement and desire into the heart; the reasoning was that this desire came from God. But since the human himself had named it nachash, and nachash means a deceiver—like a diviner who deceives and pretends, capable of showing another something that appears to come from God—he needed to guard himself against error, since he knew that error existed.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach supplies a concrete example of the misuse Rav Tzadok warns against. Adam reasons from a genuine divine gift to a mistaken permission; an already committed action and a deceptive desire compromise that reasoning. The passage therefore preserves the need to test an apparent inspiration instead of treating its claimed divine origin as sufficient. It illuminates the practical force of “the world is not worthy of this” without denying the retrospective insight reserved for repentance.

records.themeTitle: Recognizing the gift makes the work genuinely entrusted to the person
records.themeSummary: The lamp is credited as human service even while its initiating light and the power to act are acknowledged as God’s gift.
records.originHebrew: וְהָרֶמֶז הַזֶּה שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בְּנֵרוֹת הַמְּנוֹרָה, דְּאִיתָא (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה ל״ו): מֵאִיר לָעוֹלָם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהָאָרֶץ הֵאִירָה מִכְּבוֹדוֹ", וְאָמַר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל: "וְיִקְחוּ אֵלֶיךָ שֶׁמֶן וְגוֹמֵר", הֱוֵי: "לְמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיךָ תִכְסֹף", שֶׁרוֹצֶה שֶׁנָּאִיר לְפָנָיו; וְהוּא לְעֵדוּת שֶׁהַשְּׁכִינָה שׁוֹרָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי נֵר מַעֲרָבִי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא; וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁגַּם מַעֲשֵׂה מִצְוַת הַנֵּרוֹת הוּא מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁשּׁוֹלֵחַ הֶאָרָה בַּלֵּב, רַק שֶׁמְּכַנֶּה אוֹתוֹ עַל מַעֲשֵׂה הָאָדָם.
records.originEnglish: The allusion that everything comes from God is present in the menorah’s lamps. Shemot Rabbah says: He illuminates the world, as it says, ‘The earth shone with His glory,’ yet He said to Israel, ‘They shall take oil for you …’. This is ‘You long for the work of Your hands’: He wishes us to illuminate before Him. The western lamp is testimony that the Divine Presence dwells among Israel, as the Talmud says. This means that even the performance of the commandment of the lamps comes from God, who sends illumination into the heart; He simply designates it as a human action.
records.targetRef: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 15:3
records.targetHebrew: הַכַּוָּנָה כְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב הוּא: דִּמְכֻוָּון הַתּוֹרָה לִהְיוֹת הַכֹּל בְּיַד יִשְׂרָאֵל; וְזֶה לִכְאוֹרָה דֶּרֶךְ אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם הָאוֹמְרִים "כֹּחִי וְעֹצֶם יָדִי [עָשָׂה לִי אֶת הַחַיִל הַזֶּה]" (דְּבָרִים ח, יז), וְיִשְׂרָאֵל הֵם לְהֵיפֶךְ – מַכִּירִים דְּהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. רַק מִצַּד מַה שֶּׁאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתָּם שֶׁהַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת בְּיָדָם, לֹא רָצוּ לְקַבֵּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הַתּוֹרָה, הֲרֵי אַדְּרַבָּה, מַחֲשֶׁבֶת הַהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת מֵבִיא הֶעְדֵּר הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת; וְיִשְׂרָאֵל, בַּעֲלֵי הֶעְדֵּר הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת, קִבְּלוּ הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת מִזֶּה מַגִּיעַ כֵּן מִשְׁפָּטָם לִהְיוֹת נֶחְשָׁב שֶׁלָּהֶם וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יט.): "לְבַסּוֹף נִקְרֵאת תּוֹרָתוֹ".
records.targetEnglish: The intention is as stated: Torah’s purpose is that everything be in Israel’s hands. This apparently resembles the way of the nations, who say, ‘My strength and the power of my hand made this wealth for me,’ while Israel takes the opposite position, recognizing that everything comes from God. Yet because the nations, thinking that effort was in their hands, did not wish to accept the effort of Torah, their very notion of effort instead brought an absence of effort. Israel, possessing the recognition of an absence of independent effort, accepted effort. From this it follows that their claim is justified: it should be considered theirs and their effort. This is like the Sages’ statement, ‘Eventually it is called his Torah.’
records.explanation: The full Likkutei passage begins with these same Temple lamps and the divine longing for human service. Its later argument explains why acknowledgment of dependence does not erase human credit: Israel accepts work precisely while recognizing its power as given. This develops the final distinction between God’s illumination and its designation as a human act. The contrast with the nations is the author’s theological argument, not an added claim about modern populations.

records.themeTitle: Even the power to perform a commandment is received
records.themeSummary: Service can be real human work without becoming a claim of independent strength; the recognition extends even to a person’s religious achievements.
records.originHebrew: וְהָרֶמֶז הַזֶּה שֶׁהַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא בְּנֵרוֹת הַמְּנוֹרָה, דְּאִיתָא (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה ל״ו): מֵאִיר לָעוֹלָם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהָאָרֶץ הֵאִירָה מִכְּבוֹדוֹ", וְאָמַר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל: "וְיִקְחוּ אֵלֶיךָ שֶׁמֶן וְגוֹמֵר", הֱוֵי: "לְמַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיךָ תִכְסֹף", שֶׁרוֹצֶה שֶׁנָּאִיר לְפָנָיו; וְהוּא לְעֵדוּת שֶׁהַשְּׁכִינָה שׁוֹרָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי נֵר מַעֲרָבִי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא; וְהַיְנוּ שֶׁגַּם מַעֲשֵׂה מִצְוַת הַנֵּרוֹת הוּא מִצַּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁשּׁוֹלֵחַ הֶאָרָה בַּלֵּב, רַק שֶׁמְּכַנֶּה אוֹתוֹ עַל מַעֲשֵׂה הָאָדָם.
records.originEnglish: The allusion that everything comes from God is present in the menorah’s lamps. Shemot Rabbah says: He illuminates the world, as it says, ‘The earth shone with His glory,’ yet He said to Israel, ‘They shall take oil for you …’. This is ‘You long for the work of Your hands’: He wishes us to illuminate before Him. The western lamp is testimony that the Divine Presence dwells among Israel, as the Talmud says. This means that even the performance of the commandment of the lamps comes from God, who sends illumination into the heart; He simply designates it as a human action.
records.targetHebrew: שאני בשבת נאמר (שמות כ״ג:י״ב) וביום השביעי תשבות, וזה מרמז כמו שאנו אומרים וביום השביעי נתעלה וישב על כסא כבודו, והיינו שבשבת צריך האדם להכיר שאין לו שום כח פעולה, שאפילו כח הפעולה שלו הוא ג"כ מהשי"ת, שמכיר שאין לו ליקח שום תקיפות אפילו ממעשי המצות, כי זה הכח הוא ג"כ מהשי"ת. כמו שאיתא במדרש (רבה אמור כ"ז) על הפסוק (איוב מ״א:ג׳) מי הקדימני ואשלם תחת כל השמים לי הוא מי קלס לפני עד שלא נתתי בו נשמה וכו'.
records.targetEnglish: On Shabbat, by contrast, it says, ‘On the seventh day you shall cease.’ This points to what we say: ‘On the seventh day He ascended and sat upon His throne of glory.’ On Shabbat a person must recognize that he possesses no power of action independently, for even his power to act comes from God. He recognizes that he must take no confidence in his own independent strength even from the deeds of the commandments, because this power too comes from God. Thus the Midrash expounds ‘Who has preceded Me, that I should repay him? Everything under the heavens is Mine’: ‘Who praised Me before I gave him a soul?’
records.explanation: Tiferet makes Rav Tzadok’s closing point explicit at the level of religious achievement: a mitzvah does not create an exception to dependence on God. The full target first describes active weekday work that sanctifies the body and then this Shabbat recognition. The comparison therefore preserves both actual service and the refusal to claim its power as independent.

records.themeTitle: The first desire prepares an enduring personal Torah
records.themeSummary: The energy of beginning and the wisdom acquired through years of work have different roles in the enduring education recalled by Chanukah.
records.originHebrew: וְעִנְיַן "חֲנֻכָּה" הוּא הַתְחָלָה מַה שֶּׁהָאָדָם מַתְחִיל לְחַנֵּךְ עַצְמוֹ, וּמִזֶּה נִשְׁאָר קָבוּעַ לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמַּרְגִּיל עַצְמוֹ בִּתְשׁוּקָה וְרָצוֹן שֶׁל יְמֵי הַנְּעוּרִים, כְּמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "חֲנֹךְ לַנַּעַר עַל פִּי דַרְכּוֹ, גַּם כִּי יַזְקִין לֹא יָסוּר מִמֶּנָּה".
records.originEnglish: Chanukah means a beginning, when a person begins to educate himself. Through this something remains fixed for all time, as he accustoms himself through the desire and will of his youthful days, as it says: ‘Educate the youth according to his way; even when he grows old, he will not depart from it.’
records.targetHebrew: הַהַתְחָלָה לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא הַחֵשֶׁק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי אִם בְּתוֹרַת ה' חֶפְצוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים א, ב), וְאָז נִקְרָא תּוֹרַת ה' כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה (יט.), וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַהַשָּׂגָה שֶׁנִּקְרָא "וּבְתוֹרָתוֹ יֶהְגֶּה וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם). וְהַחֵשֶׁק גָּדוֹל יוֹתֵר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל פָּסוּק "טוֹב שֵׁם מִשֶּׁמֶן טוֹב" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, א) וְעַל מַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: גְּדוֹלָה שִׁמּוּשָׁהּ וְכוּלֵי (בְּרָכוֹת ז:). וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם זֶהוּ בַּהַתְחָלָה וּבְיַלְדוּת שֶׁאָז הַחֵשֶׁק גּוֹבֵר, וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ שִׁילְהֵי שַׁבָּת (קנב.): יַנְקוּתָא כְּלִילָא דְּוַרְדָּא וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם שְׁבַח הַיַּלְדוּת וּגְנוּת הַזִּקְנָה שֶׁאָז הַחֵשֶׁק כָּבָה. וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: זִקְנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים וְכוּלֵי, וְכִי בְּכָל מָקוֹם נִשְׁתַּבְּחוּ זְקֵנִים, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּשְׁמוֹת רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה ה) וּבְוַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה (סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה יא), דְּבֶאֱמֶת אָמְרוּ (תַּעֲנִית ז.): הַרְבֵּה לָמַדְתִּי מֵרַבּוֹתַי וְכוּלֵי וּמִתַּלְמִידַי יוֹתֵר וְכוּלֵי, וּמֵרַבּוֹתַי הַיְינוּ הַהַתְחָלָה וְהַחֵשֶׁק. וְאַחַר פְּטִירַת הָרַב, וְנִקְרָא "תּוֹרָתוֹ" שֶׁיָּגַע מֵעַצְמוֹ לְלַמֵּד לַאֲחֵרִים, אָז לָמַד יוֹתֵר וּמוֹסִיפִים חָכְמָה, רַק שֶׁהַהַשָּׂגָה הוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי "ה' יִתֵּן חָכְמָה", וְהַכֹּל בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם חוּץ מִיִּרְאַת שָׁמַיִם שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת הַנּוּקְבָא וְהָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא בְּחֵשֶׁק וְרָצוֹן כַּנּוֹדָע, זֶהוּ בִּידֵי אָדָם, לְכָךְ זֶהוּ טוֹב וְגָדוֹל.
records.targetEnglish: The beginning of words of Torah is desire, as it says, ‘His desire is in the Torah of the Lord.’ Then it is called the Lord’s Torah, as in Avodah Zarah 19a; afterwards comes attainment, called ‘and in his Torah he meditates.’ Desire is greater, as I heard concerning ‘A good name is better than good oil’ and the Sages’ saying that serving Torah scholars is greater than studying. Nevertheless, this is at the beginning and in youth, when desire is strong. Thus the end of Shabbat says, ‘Youth is a garland of roses …’; see there its praise of youth and its unfavorable description of old age, when desire is extinguished. Yet the Sages also praise aged Torah scholars, and elders are praised elsewhere. In truth they said, ‘I learned much from my teachers … and from my students more …’. ‘From my teachers’ refers to the beginning and desire. After the teacher’s passing, when it is called ‘his Torah’ because he toils himself to teach others, he then learns more and increases wisdom. Attainment, however, comes from God, for ‘the Lord gives wisdom,’ and everything is in Heaven’s hands except fear of Heaven. The latter is the receptive, feminine attribute and the awakening from below through desire and will; it is in the person’s hands, and therefore is good and great.
records.explanation: Tzidkat distinguishes the beginning’s strong desire from later attainment gained through teaching and toil. This explains what can remain from youthful education even as a person’s learning matures. The comparison does not require an older learner to reproduce exactly the emotional intensity of the first encounter; the complete target also values the later personal acquisition of Torah.

records.themeTitle: The first taste grows through sustained desire
records.themeSummary: Education endures because desire develops the initial seed of Torah into repeatedly renewed understanding.
records.originHebrew: וְעִנְיַן "חֲנֻכָּה" הוּא הַתְחָלָה מַה שֶּׁהָאָדָם מַתְחִיל לְחַנֵּךְ עַצְמוֹ, וּמִזֶּה נִשְׁאָר קָבוּעַ לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד עַל יְדֵי שֶׁמַּרְגִּיל עַצְמוֹ בִּתְשׁוּקָה וְרָצוֹן שֶׁל יְמֵי הַנְּעוּרִים, כְּמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "חֲנֹךְ לַנַּעַר עַל פִּי דַרְכּוֹ, גַּם כִּי יַזְקִין לֹא יָסוּר מִמֶּנָּה".
records.originEnglish: Chanukah means a beginning, when a person begins to educate himself. Through this something remains fixed for all time, as he accustoms himself through the desire and will of his youthful days, as it says: ‘Educate the youth according to his way; even when he grows old, he will not depart from it.’
records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Bereshit 15
records.targetHebrew: זֶה סֵפֶר תּוֹלְדוֹת אָדָם בִּדְמוּת אֱלֹקִים עָשָׂה וְכוּלֵי. סוֹד הָעִנְיָן צֶלֶם וּדְמוּת, צֶלֶם הַיְינוּ גוּף הַחַיִּים בְּלִי שׁוּם הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת כְּמוֹ תִּינוֹק תֵּכֶף כְּשֶׁנּוֹלַד בָּרֶגַע הָרִאשׁוֹן יִקָּרֵא צֶלֶם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר יַתְחִיל לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט בִּרְצוֹנוֹתָיו כְּגוֹן תְּשִׁיקוּת הָאֲכִילָה וְעַל יְדֵי אוֹתָהּ הַתְּשׁוּקָה הוּא אוֹכֵל, וְנִתְגַּדֵּל אֶצְלוֹ הַחַיִּים בְּכָל פַּעַם יוֹתֵר וְיוֹתֵר עַד שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה גָּדוֹל בְּעוֹבִי וְקוֹמָה, זֹאת הַהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת יִקָּרֵא דְּמוּת. וּכְמוֹ כֵן בְּנֶפֶשׁ הַטִּיפָּה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁנִּכְנֶסֶת בָּאָדָם יִקָּרֵא צֶלֶם, וְהַתְּשׁוּקָה שֶׁמִּשְׁתּוֹקֵק לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה יִקָּרֵא דְּמוּת וְעַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּקָה נִתּוֹסֵף לוֹ בְּכָל פַּעַם יוֹתֵר דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְזֶה "בְּיוֹם בְּרוֹא אֱלֹקִים אָדָם בִּדְמוּת אֱלֹקִים" וְכוּלֵי, הַיְינוּ כִּי זֶה הָיָה עִקָּר בְּרִיאַת הָאָדָם בִּכְדֵי שֶׁיִּשְׁתּוֹקֵק בְּכָל פַּעַם לְהִתְרַבּוּת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְזֶה עִנְיַן (בְּרָכוֹת ז:) גָּדוֹל שִׁמּוּשָׁהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה יוֹתֵר מִלִּמּוּדָהּ, שִׁמּוּשָׁהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה נִקְרֵאת הַתְּשׁוּקָה. וְזֶה פֵּירוּשׁ "זֶה סֵפֶר תּוֹלְדוֹת אָדָם" הַיְינוּ שֶׁאִם יִזְכֶּה הָאָדָם לִהְיוֹת בְּצֶלֶם וּדְמוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר, יִרְאֶה בְּכָל פַּעַם הִתְחַדְּשׁוּת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְיִסְפּוֹר שָׁנָיו וְתוֹלְדוֹתָיו וְיַאֲרִיךְ יָמִים.
records.targetEnglish: ‘This is the book of the generations of the human; in the likeness of God He made …’. The inner meaning of image and likeness is this: image is life itself without any expansion. A baby immediately upon birth, in its first moment, is called image. Afterwards, when it begins to extend itself through its desires—for example the desire to eat, through which it eats—its life continually increases until it grows in breadth and stature. This expansion is called likeness. So too in the soul: the first drop of Torah that enters a person is called image, and the desire with which he longs for Torah is called likeness. Through desire, more Torah is continually added to him. This is ‘On the day God created the human, in the likeness of God …’: the essential purpose of the human’s creation was that he should continually desire an increase of Torah. This is ‘Serving Torah is greater than studying it’: serving Torah is called desire. ‘This is the book of the generations of the human’ means that if he merits image and likeness in this way, he will continually see renewal in Torah, count his years and generations, and lengthen his days.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach gives a developmental account of the lasting beginning: a first drop is not the full stature, and desire is what continually grows it. This illuminates Rav Tzadok’s use of a youth’s education as the model for a dedication whose Torah light remains through later years.

records.themeTitle: Torah’s ancestral stages refine how it is transmitted
records.themeSummary: The movement from Abraham’s expansive teaching through Isaac’s restraint to Jacob’s completeness explains distinct stages within the same Torah light.
records.originHebrew: דְּהִנֵּה עִנְיַן שִׁבְעַת הַנֵּרוֹת שֶׁל הַמְּנוֹרָה מְרַמְּזִים עַל הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת אוֹר הַתּוֹרָה בְּכָל שֶׁבַע הַמִּדּוֹת הַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת נֶגֶד שִׁבְעַת הָרוֹעִים שֶׁהֵם מֶרְכָּבָה לְשֶׁבַע הַמִּדּוֹת, וּבְכֻלָּם נִמְצָא הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה הַמְּרֻמָּז לַמְּנוֹרָה בַּדָּרוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא כ״ה עַמּוּד ב׳): "הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁיַּחְכִּים יַדְרִים וְכוּלֵיהּ". וְהַיְנוּ כִּי בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם אִיתָא (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס״א) שֶׁזִּמֵּן לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שְׁנֵי כִלְיוֹתָיו כִּשְׁנֵי רַבָּנִים וְהָיוּ נוֹבְעוֹת וּמְלַמְּדוֹת אוֹתוֹ חָכְמָה, וְגַם הַשְּׁנֵי אֲלָפִים תּוֹרָה הִתְחִילוּ מֵאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם. וּבְיִצְחָק אִיתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג׳ פ׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳): "אוֹרַיְּתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִּגְבוּרָה קָאָתְיָא", שֶׁהִיא יִרְאָה מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל יִצְחָק, וְכָל מַה שֶּׁנִּתְפַּשְּׁטָה יוֹתֵר חָכְמַת הַתּוֹרָה בְּהַמִּדּוֹת הוּא בְּתֹקֶף הִתְלַהֲבוּת בְּיוֹתֵר. וּבְיַעֲקֹב שֶׁמִּדָּתוֹ אֱמֶת נִתְפַּשְּׁטָה הֶאָרַת הַתּוֹרָה בְּיוֹתֵר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): "אֱמֶת זוֹ תּוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'אֱמֶת קְנֵה וְאַל תִּמְכֹּר'".
records.originEnglish: The menorah’s seven lamps allude to the spread of Torah’s light through all seven holy attributes, corresponding to the seven shepherds who embody them. The wisdom of Torah spreads through them all, as indicated by the menorah in the south: ‘One who wishes to become wise should turn southward.’ Bereshit Rabbah says that God provided Abraham with his two kidneys as two teachers, which flowed and taught him wisdom; the two thousand years of Torah also began with Abraham. Concerning Isaac, ‘Torah comes from the side of might’—fear, Isaac’s attribute. The more Torah’s wisdom spreads through the attributes, the more intense its flame. In Jacob, whose attribute is truth, Torah’s illumination spread still further: ‘Truth means Torah, as it says, “Acquire truth and do not sell it.”’
records.targetHebrew: וְהוּא הַתְחָלַת הִתְגַּלּוּת הַתּוֹרָה, דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִגְבוּרָה נָפְקָא (כְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב׳ פָּרָשַׁת [בֹּא] ס׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד ב׳); כִּי בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, אַף דְּהוּא עַצְמוֹ קִיֵּם כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ (כְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹמָא כ״ח עַמּוּד ב׳) וּשְׁתֵּי כִלְיוֹתָיו הָיוּ נוֹבְעוֹת תּוֹרָה (כְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ס״א [ס״א:א׳]), מִכָּל מָקוֹם עִקַּר שֵׁם "תּוֹרָה" לְשׁוֹן הוֹרָאָה, שֶׁמּוֹרֶה דֶּרֶךְ לַאֲחֵרִים, זֶה לֹא נִתְבָּרֵר עֲדַיִן בְּאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, שֶׁלְּכָל אוֹתָן שֶׁלִּמֵּד לֹא נִשְׁאַר בָּהֶם כְּלוּם, רַק מַה שֶּׁלִּמֵּד אַחַר כָּךְ לִבְנוֹ יִצְחָק זֶה נִשְׁאַר קַיָּם לָעַד. וּבְיִצְחָק לֹא מָצִינוּ עוֹד "נֶפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה" וְשֶׁלִּמֵּד לַאֲחֵרִים, שֶׁכְּבָר הָיָה בּוֹ כֹּחַ הַצִּמְצוּם, לְצַמְצֵם הַהַשְׁפָּעָה שֶׁלֹּא לְלַמֵּד וּלְהַשְׁפִּיעַ תּוֹרַת חֶסֶד לַחִיצוֹנִים וּלְשֶׁאֵין רְאוּיִים לָהּ, וְלֹא לִמֵּד אֶלָּא לְבָנָיו. וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם גַּם בָּהֶם הָיָה שֶׁאֵין רָאוּי, אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּקְרָא "יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר" בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (י״ח עַמּוּד א׳), שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ שֹׁרֶשׁ יַהֲדוּת מִלֵּדָה, דְּעַל כֵּן רֹאשׁוֹ קָבוּר בִּמְעָרַת הַמַּכְפֵּלָה בְּעִטְפֵּיהּ דְּיִצְחָק (תַּרְגּוּם יוֹנָתָן וַיְחִי נ׳:י״ג), עַל שֵׁם "הַצַּיִד בְּפִיו" [בְּרֵאשִׁית כ״ה:כ״ח], דְּנַפְשׁוֹת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר שָׁרְשֵׁי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה [דְּהַמִּשְׁנָיוֹת יְסוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה: סְתַם מִשְׁנָה — רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְכֻלְּהוּ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא כַּנּוֹדָע], וְעַל כֵּן גַּם בּוֹ הָיָה קְצָת אֲחִיזָה לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם סוֹף סוֹף הָיָה פְּסֹלֶת גַּם כֵּן. וּשְׁלֵמוּת הַתּוֹרָה הָיָה בְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁמִּטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵמָה, שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵמוּת מִדַּת "אֱמֶת", זוֹ תּוֹרָה [בְּרָכוֹת ה׳ עַמּוּד ב׳]. וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם מִסִּטְרָא דִגְבוּרָה נָפְקָא, כְּבָר הֵחֵל שֹׁרֶשׁ הַיְּצִיאָה בְּיִצְחָק.
records.targetEnglish: Isaac is the beginning of Torah’s disclosure, for Torah comes forth from the side of might. Although Abraham himself fulfilled the whole Torah and his two kidneys flowed with Torah, the principal meaning of the name Torah is instruction, directing a way for others. This was not yet clarified in Abraham, for nothing remained among all those he taught. Only what he later taught his son Isaac endured forever. In Isaac we find no further ‘souls that he made’ and taught to others, because the power of restraint was already within him: to limit the outflow, so as not to teach and bestow a Torah of kindness upon those outside or unworthy of it. He taught only his children. Yet even among them was one unworthy, although he is called an apostate Israelite in Kiddushin 18a: he possessed a Jewish root from birth. Thus his head is buried in the Cave of Machpelah in Isaac’s bosom, on account of ‘the game in his mouth’: the souls of Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Meir, roots of Oral Torah. The Mishnah is the foundation of Oral Torah; an anonymous Mishnah is Rabbi Meir, and all follow Rabbi Akiva’s approach. Thus even within him there was some attachment to Torah, but ultimately there was refuse as well. Torah’s completeness was in Jacob, whose offspring were whole: completeness in truth, which is Torah. Nevertheless, it comes forth from the side of might; the root of that emergence had already begun in Isaac.
records.explanation: Poked explains the succession that the origin names: Abraham’s knowledge expands, Isaac gives it a bounded line of transmission, and Jacob brings that line to completeness. It therefore clarifies the function of might and truth within the spread of Torah, rather than treating the three patriarchs as interchangeable holders of knowledge. Its statements about the earlier pupils and Esau’s spiritual roots remain the author’s interpretive account.

Clarified antecedents and grammatical referents are integrated into the English; original authorial asides remain explicit; the relation explanation is editorial and is not part of the quotation.

records.themeTitle: Torah reveals why restraint itself can serve kindness
records.themeSummary: The statement that Torah emerges from might describes the stage of concealment and effort; later understanding sees the kindness within that very concealment.

records.targetHebrew: וזה נקרא אוריאן תליתאי, כי מה תורה דאורי וגלי במה דהוה סתים דלא אתידע כדאיתא בזוה"ק (מצורע נג:), כי תליתאי נקרא אחר שבא האדם בחזרה אל החסד הראשון על ידי עבודתו. ואף שאיתא בזוה"ק (קדושים פ:) אורייתא מסטרא דגבורה נפקת, זה הכל קודם שבוקע את ההעלם, אז נדמה לו שאורו של השי"ת וההעלם הם שני הפכיים, וזה מורה מסטרא דגבורה נפקת, אבל אח"כ רואה באמת שהכל הוא בחסדו, שגם ההעלם הזה הוא מחמת שהשי"ת הוא רב חסד, ורצה שיהיה לאדם חלק בעבודתו אשר הוא עובד, לזה העלים השי"ת ממנו את החסד הזה כדי שיהיה מקום לעבודה ואז נקרא אוריאן תליתאי.
records.targetEnglish: This is called the threefold Torah. For Torah is what instructs and reveals what had been hidden and unknown, as the Zohar says. ‘Threefold’ means that the person has returned through his work to the first kindness. Although the Zohar says that Torah comes forth from the side of might, this is before he breaks through the concealment. Then it seems to him that God’s light and concealment are two opposites; this is ‘it comes forth from the side of might.’ Afterwards he sees that everything is in truth His kindness. The concealment too exists because God is abundantly kind and wanted the person to have a share in the service he performs. Therefore He hid that kindness from him so that there would be room for work. Then it is called the threefold Torah.
records.explanation: Tiferet expounds the same phrase about Torah emerging from might and explains its place within a three-stage movement. This makes the origin’s growth from Abraham’s kindness through Isaac’s fear more intelligible: the restriction creates room for acquired understanding, and that understanding can reveal the kindness within it. The target’s final discussion also distinguishes Abraham’s personal attainment from its fixed inheritance after three generations.

records.themeTitle: The sown light produces more Torah within the heart
records.themeSummary: The righteous person’s seed of light is explained as written Torah giving rise to a much larger growth of Oral Torah.
records.originHebrew: וּבְיוֹסֵף כְּתִיב: "כִּי בֶן זְקֻנִים הוּא לוֹ", וְאִיתָא בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה: שֶׁכָּל הֲלָכוֹת שֶׁמָּסְרוּ שֵׁם וָעֵבֶר לְיַעֲקֹב מְסָרָן לוֹ; וְגַם אָמְרוּ (תַּעֲנִית ט״ו עַמּוּד א׳): "צַדִּיקִים לְאוֹרָה", דִּכְתִיב: "אוֹר זָרֻעַ לַצַּדִּיק", וְעַל יְדֵי הָאוֹר הַזָּרוּעַ בִּבְחִינַת צַדִּיק נִשְׁפַּע וְנִתְפַּשֵּׁט הֶאָרַת הַתּוֹרָה בְּשֶׁפַע רַב כַּיָּדוּעַ.
records.originEnglish: Concerning Joseph it is written, ‘For he was a son of old age to him’; Bereshit Rabbah says that all the teachings Shem and Ever transmitted to Jacob, he transmitted to Joseph. They also said, ‘The righteous are destined for light,’ as it says, ‘Light is sown for the righteous.’ Through the light sown in the aspect of the righteous one, the illumination of Torah flows and spreads in great abundance.
records.targetHebrew: פֵּירוּשׁ, צַדִּיק הוּא הַמּוּגְדָּר בְּמַעֲשָׂיו, אַף שֶׁהַלֵּב אֵינוֹ שָׁלֵם וְיָשָׁר עֲדַיִן, מִכָּל מָקוֹם מַגְבִּיר שִׂכְלוֹ עַל יִצְרוֹ לְבִלְתִּי יִגָּרֵר אַחֲרָיו, וְזָהִיר בְּמַעֲשֶׂה בַּפּוֹעַל כָּל רְמַ"ח (מָאתַיִם אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה) מִצְווֹת עֲשֵׂה וּשְׁסָ"ה (שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת שִׁשִּׁים וְחָמֵשׁ) מִצְווֹת לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה. וְהַמַּעֲשִׂים מְבִיאִים קְדוּשָּׁה לַלֵּב, דְּעַל כֵּן מְבָרְכִין "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו", פֵּירוּשׁ, קְדוּשָּׁה בְּכָל מָקוֹם הוּא הַבְדָּלָה, לְהַבְדִּיל וּלְהַפְרִישׁ הַלֵּב מֵחֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה; וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה לָאוֹר הַזָּרוּעַ, שֶׁהוּא הַשָּׂגַת חִידּוּשִׁין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מִתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַמְּאִירִים לַלֵּב. כִּי "אוֹרָה" – זוֹ תּוֹרָה, וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הִיא "הָאֱמֶת אֲשֶׁר מֵאֶרֶץ תִּצְמָח", שֶׁהִיא כִּזְרִיעָה בְּלִבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, לְהַצְמִיחַ מִתּוֹךְ לְבָבָם הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד תּוֹסֶפֶת מְרוּבָּה עַל הָעִיקָּר. וּכְמַאן דְּאָמַר בְּגִיטִּין (ס:): "רוֹב תּוֹרָה בְּעַל פֶּה", וְגַם מַאן דְּאָמַר "רוּבָּהּ בִּכְתָב" לֹא פָּלֵיג אַמְּצִיאוּת, רַק סְבִירָא לֵיהּ כֵּיוָון דְּלֵיכָּא מִידֵי דְּלָא רְמִיזֵי בְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וְהַכֹּל נִדְרָשׁ מִתּוֹךְ הַכְּתוּבִים, וְכֵיוָון דְּאִתְיְהִיב לְמִידְרַשׁ כְּמַאן דִּכְתִיב מְפוֹרָשׁ דָּמֵי, קָרֵי לֵיהּ "רוֹב בִּכְתָב", וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה כָּתְבוּ הַמְּפָרְשִׁים. אֲבָל וַדַּאי עַצְמוּת הַכְּתָב דָּבָר מוּעָט מְאֹד, וְעִיקַּר מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (אִיּוֹב יא, ט): "אֲרֻכָּה מֵאֶרֶץ מִדָּהּ" הוּא מִצַּד בֵּיאוּרָהּ שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הַנִּצְמָח מִלִּבְבוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי אוֹר שֶׁבִּכְתָב הַזָּרוּעַ בָּהֶם.
records.targetEnglish: A righteous person is one whose actions are bounded: even if the heart is not yet whole and upright, he strengthens his understanding over his inclination so as not to be drawn after it, and is careful in practice with all 248 positive and 365 negative commandments. Deeds bring holiness to the heart; hence we bless, ‘Who sanctified us with His commandments.’ Holiness means separation: separating the heart from the desires of this world. Through this he attains the sown light—new understandings of Oral Torah that illuminate the heart. For ‘light’ is Torah, and Written Torah is ‘the truth that sprouts from the earth’: it is sown in Israel’s hearts to grow from them a very great addition, much greater than the original seed. This accords with the view in Gittin 60b that most Torah is oral. Even the view that most is written does not dispute the reality; it holds that because nothing is without an allusion in Torah and everything is expounded from the verses, permission to expound it makes it as though explicitly written. Yet the written text itself is certainly small in extent, and ‘its measure is longer than the earth’ applies chiefly to its oral explanation growing from Israel’s hearts through the written light sown within them.
records.explanation: Resisei interprets the very light/ righteous-person saying quoted here and explains both the soil and the growth: disciplined deeds prepare the heart, and the written seed yields expanding oral explanation. This supplies a precise meaning for the origin’s “great abundance.” The full target’s later distinction between light and joy was read; the quotation does not equate bounded action with already completed inner uprightness.

records.themeTitle: David’s inward understanding opens a nonprophetic teaching lineage
records.themeSummary: The Davidic connection to Oral Torah is explained through understanding in the heart, repentance, and the spread of teaching through large circles of students.
records.originHebrew: וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת, "פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לַהּ".
records.originEnglish: King David embodies the attribute of kingship: ‘the mouth, which we call Oral Torah.’
records.targetHebrew: [צג] וְיָדוּעַ דִּכְמוֹ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ ע״ה הָיָה רַבָּן שֶׁל כָּל הַנְּבִיאִים, כֵּן הָיָה דָּוִד רַבָּן שֶׁל כָּל בַּעֲלֵי רוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ וּמִמֶּנּוּ הַתְחָלַת הִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת הַרְבָּצַת הַתּוֹרָה וְהַחָכְמָה בִּישִׁיבוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת וְתַלְמִידִים רַבִּים שֶׁלֹּא עַל יְדֵי נְבוּאָה, וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הַבִּינָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה בָּא לַהֲקָמַת עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה וּבְדוֹר רַבִּי נִתְבָּרְרוּ כָּל הַשֵּׁשׁ קְצָווֹת דְּמִדַּת הַתְּשׁוּבָה, שֶׁהֵם כָּל הַכֹּחוֹת שֶׁבְּכֹחַ כּוּלָּם וְעַל כֵּן נִתְגַּלָּה אָז כְּלָלוּת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה בְּחִבּוּר הַמִּשְׁנָה, דְּכוֹלֶלֶת בְּכֹחַ גַּם כָּל מַה שֶּׁיִּתְחַדֵּשׁ מֵחַכְמֵי הַדּוֹרוֹת אַחַר כָּךְ
records.targetEnglish: Just as Moses was the master of all prophets, David was the master of all who possessed holy inspiration. With him began the spread of teaching Torah and wisdom in great academies with many students, through a means other than prophecy. This came through the awakening of understanding in the heart, from which he came to establish the yoke of repentance. In Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi’s generation, all six directions of the attribute of repentance were clarified—all the powers potentially contained within them. Therefore the totality of Oral Torah was then revealed in the composition of the Mishnah, which potentially includes everything that later generations’ sages will innovate.
records.explanation: Takanat explains the terse identification of David, mouth, and Oral Torah through a particular mode of teaching: understanding awakens in the heart and spreads without being a prophetic message. Its contrast with Moses and its continuation to Rabbi’s Mishnah make the distinct roles named in Rav Tzadok’s paragraph concrete. This is the author’s account of the spiritual roots of those teaching lineages.

records.themeTitle: Moses’ direct illumination still has a task to perform
records.themeSummary: The reference to Moses as Torah’s root can be illuminated through his unhidden perception of divine light and the service that remains even at that height.
records.originHebrew: וּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן הֵמָּה הַשֹּׁרֶשׁ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה. וְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת, "פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לַהּ".
records.originEnglish: Moses and Aaron are the roots of Written Torah and Oral Torah. King David embodies the attribute of kingship: ‘the mouth, which we call Oral Torah.’
records.targetHebrew: וזה שאיתא במה שימש משה וכו' היינו דבמשה כתיב שהיה כבד פה וכבד לשון. וביאר בזה כבוד אזמו"ר הגה"ק זללה"ה, שאיתא בש"ס (נדה ל:) בשעה שבא אדם לעולם בא מלאך וסטרו על פיו ושוכח מה שלמד, דבשעה שהוא במעי אמו הוא רואה האור מפורש, כמו שכתיב (איוב כ״ט:ב׳-ג׳) מי יתנני כירחי קדם כימי אלוה ישמרנו בהלו נרו עלי ראשו וגו', ואח"כ כשבא לעולם בא מלאך וסטרו על פיו ושוכח מה שלמד, היינו שמסתיר ממנו אור השי"ת, ובמשה לא היה סטרו על פיו, והיה רואה מפורש האור של השי"ת, ע"כ נקרא כבד פה וכבד לשון. וזה פריך הגמ' במה שימש משה, היינו מה היה העבודה שלו, הרי משרע"ה היה בתכלית השלימות והיה רואה האור מפורש, וכמו שאיתא בש"ס (ראש השנה כא:) נ' שערי בינה נבראו בעולם וכולן נתנו למשה חסר אחד, וכמו שכתיב (בראשית ו׳:ג׳) בשגם הוא בשר, ואיתא בש"ס (חולין קלט:) בשגם זה משה, ואמר בזה כבוד אזמו"ר הגה"ק זללה"ה שמזה הוא ראיה שהיה גדול שבנבראים. ומה היה העבודה שלו, ומסיק בחלוק לבן שאין לו אימרא. אימרא הוא לשון שפה, היינו שעבודת משרע"ה היה רק להראות לישראל שאין בעוה"ז שום שלימות, שאפילו מי שהוא בתכלית השלימות צריך ג"כ לעבודה, כמו שאיתא במדרש (רבה שמות מב) לך רד כי שחת עמך אתה והם בירידה, היינו שהיו מראין לו שאין בעוה"ז שום שלימות, וזה יהיה נתקן לעתיד וכמו שאיתא בזוה"ק, עתיד משה ליחדא קוב"ה עם כנסת ישראל כחדא:
records.targetEnglish: This is the question, ‘In what did Moses serve?’ Concerning Moses it is written that he was heavy of mouth and tongue. My holy grandfather explained: the Talmud says that when a person comes into the world, an angel strikes his mouth and he forgets what he learned. In his mother’s womb he sees the light explicitly, as it says, ‘Would that I were as in earlier months … when His lamp shone over my head.’ Afterwards, at his entry into the world, the angel strikes his mouth and he forgets: God’s light is concealed from him. With Moses there was no striking of his mouth, and he saw God’s light explicitly; therefore he is called heavy of mouth and tongue. Thus the Talmud asks, ‘In what did Moses serve?’ What was his service, since he was at the height of completeness and saw the light explicitly? The Talmud says that fifty gates of understanding were created and all but one were given to Moses. ‘For he too is flesh’—beshaggam—is expounded as Moses; my holy grandfather said that this proves he was the greatest of created beings. What, then, was his service? It answers: in a white robe without a hem. Imra means an edge or lip: Moses’ service was to show Israel that nothing in this world is complete, so that even someone at the height of completeness still needs service. Thus the Midrash says, ‘Go down, for your people have become corrupt’: you and they are in descent. They were showing him that nothing in this world is complete. This will be repaired in the future, as the Zohar says: Moses will unite the Holy One and the congregation of Israel as one.
records.explanation: Tiferet develops the Moses component of the origin’s list: direct illumination differs from the concealed light normally recovered through learning. It also asks what work remains for Moses, preventing a reading in which being a root of Torah means having no further service. The comparison does not claim that this target restates the origin’s complete assignment of all seven figures.

records.themeTitle: Longing builds a vessel within the heart
records.themeSummary: The menorah as a receiving vessel is illuminated by the connection between heartfelt desire and the inner dwelling of the Divine Presence.
records.originHebrew: וּבַחֲנֻכָּה מַדְלִיקִין שְׁמוֹנָה נֵרוֹת, כִּי הַנֵּר שְׁמִינִי מְרַמֵּז עַל בִּינָה לִבָּא, שֶׁהוּא הַמָּקוֹר שֶׁל שִׁבְעַת הָאוֹרוֹת הַנִּזְכָּרִים, וְהַיְנוּ הַתְּשׁוּקָה וְהָרָצוֹן שֶׁבַּלֵּב לְהַגִּיעַ לִמְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁתִּתְפַּשֵּׁט בַּלֵּב. וְעִקַּר הַגַּעְגּוּעִים וְהַתְּשׁוּקָה בַּלֵּב לִזְכּוֹת לִמְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה נִתְגַּלָּה אָז בִּימֵי גְּזֵרַת יָוָן, שֶׁהָיָה לְבַטְּלָם מִתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת; וְהָיָה לִבָּם נִשְׁבָּר מְאֹד מִזֶּה, שֶׁנִּרְאֶה שֶׁמִּן הַשָּׁמַיִם מְעַכְּבִין מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין הַתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם מְקֻבָּל בְּעֵינָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהוּא דּוֹמֶה כְּשׁוֹפֵךְ קִיתוֹן עַל פָּנָיו (בְּסֻכָּה). וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְמַרְמְרוּ וְגָדְלָה הַתְּשׁוּקָה בְּלִבָּם לַעֲסֹק בַּתּוֹרָה בַּסֵּתֶר; וְגַם אוֹתָם שֶׁלֹּא יָכְלוּ לְהַצְנִיעַ עַצְמָם וְלַעֲסֹק בַּתּוֹרָה, עוֹד יוֹתֵר גָּדְלָה הַצְּעָקָה וְהַתְּשׁוּקָה בְּלִבָּם לִזְכּוֹת לִמְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לְנֵס שֶׁנִּזְדַּמֵּן לָהֶם הַשַּׁפּוּדִין שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל לַעֲשׂוֹת הַמְּנוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא הַכְּלִי קִבּוּל לִמְאוֹר שִׁבְעַת הַנֵּרוֹת, שֶׁהִיא כְּנֶגֶד הָרָצוֹן שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה כְּלִי לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁפָּע בּוֹ מְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה.
records.originEnglish: On Chanukah we light eight lamps. The eighth alludes to understanding in the heart, the source of the seven lights mentioned above: the heart’s longing and will to reach the illumination of Torah so that it spreads within the heart. The deepest yearning to attain Torah’s light was revealed in the days of the Greek decree, which sought to abolish Torah and commandments. Their hearts were greatly broken by this: it seemed that Heaven was preventing them because their Torah and commandments were not accepted before God, like a servant whose pitcher is poured back into his face. Through this they grew bitter and their hearts’ longing to study Torah in secret increased. Even those who could not hide themselves and study had an even greater cry and longing within their hearts to attain Torah’s light. Through this they merited the miracle of finding iron spits to make the menorah, the vessel receiving the light of the seven lamps. It corresponds to the will in the heart, through which a vessel is made to receive Torah’s illumination.
records.targetHebrew: עַל יְדֵי הַחֵשֶׁק הוּא כְּלִי קִבּוּל לְהַשְׁרָאַת שְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּקֶרֶב לִבּוֹ. וְזֶהוּ תְּרוּמַת הַמִּשְׁכָּן: "מֵאֵת כָּל אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִדְּבֶנּוּ לִבּוֹ" (שְׁמוֹת כה, ב), דִּנְדִיבוּת הַלֵּב דִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי זֶה הוּא בִּנְיַן הַמִּשְׁכָּן דִּשְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים. וּבָזֶה הוּא כָּל חַד לְפוּם מַה דִּמְשַׁעֵר בְּלִבֵּיהּ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה הַרְגָּשַׁת אֶחָד מִשְׁכַּן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלִבּוֹ לַחֲבֵירוֹ; כִּי כְּפִי נְדִיבַת לְבָבוֹ בְּתִגְבּוֹרֶת חֶשְׁקוֹ לְהַשִּׂיג, כָּךְ הוּא שְׁכִינַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
records.targetEnglish: Through desire, a person becomes a vessel for the Divine Presence to dwell within his heart. This is the contribution for the Tabernacle: ‘From every person whose heart moves him.’ Through Israel’s generous heart the Tabernacle is built, the dwelling of the Divine Presence below. In this, each person is according to what he measures within his heart: one person’s awareness of God’s dwelling in his heart is unlike another’s. According to his heart’s generosity, in the strengthening of his desire to attain, so is the dwelling of the Divine Presence.
records.explanation: Tzidkat explains the vessel metaphor in terms of a person’s capacity to receive, not merely an external object that holds oil. Its full continuation distinguishes the differing measures of positive attainment from everyone’s obligation and capacity to remove evil. That distinction preserves the specific claim about desire without making every kind of desire spiritually sufficient.

records.themeTitle: Sincere longing has value before learning bears visible fruit
records.themeSummary: Those prevented from attaining Torah still form a real relation to it through sustained, unresentful desire and effort.
records.originHebrew: וּבַחֲנֻכָּה מַדְלִיקִין שְׁמוֹנָה נֵרוֹת, כִּי הַנֵּר שְׁמִינִי מְרַמֵּז עַל בִּינָה לִבָּא, שֶׁהוּא הַמָּקוֹר שֶׁל שִׁבְעַת הָאוֹרוֹת הַנִּזְכָּרִים, וְהַיְנוּ הַתְּשׁוּקָה וְהָרָצוֹן שֶׁבַּלֵּב לְהַגִּיעַ לִמְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁתִּתְפַּשֵּׁט בַּלֵּב. וְעִקַּר הַגַּעְגּוּעִים וְהַתְּשׁוּקָה בַּלֵּב לִזְכּוֹת לִמְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה נִתְגַּלָּה אָז בִּימֵי גְּזֵרַת יָוָן, שֶׁהָיָה לְבַטְּלָם מִתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת; וְהָיָה לִבָּם נִשְׁבָּר מְאֹד מִזֶּה, שֶׁנִּרְאֶה שֶׁמִּן הַשָּׁמַיִם מְעַכְּבִין מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין הַתּוֹרָה וּמִצְווֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם מְקֻבָּל בְּעֵינָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהוּא דּוֹמֶה כְּשׁוֹפֵךְ קִיתוֹן עַל פָּנָיו (בְּסֻכָּה). וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִתְמַרְמְרוּ וְגָדְלָה הַתְּשׁוּקָה בְּלִבָּם לַעֲסֹק בַּתּוֹרָה בַּסֵּתֶר; וְגַם אוֹתָם שֶׁלֹּא יָכְלוּ לְהַצְנִיעַ עַצְמָם וְלַעֲסֹק בַּתּוֹרָה, עוֹד יוֹתֵר גָּדְלָה הַצְּעָקָה וְהַתְּשׁוּקָה בְּלִבָּם לִזְכּוֹת לִמְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לְנֵס שֶׁנִּזְדַּמֵּן לָהֶם הַשַּׁפּוּדִין שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל לַעֲשׂוֹת הַמְּנוֹרָה שֶׁהִיא הַכְּלִי קִבּוּל לִמְאוֹר שִׁבְעַת הַנֵּרוֹת, שֶׁהִיא כְּנֶגֶד הָרָצוֹן שֶׁבַּלֵּב שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה כְּלִי לִהְיוֹת נִשְׁפָּע בּוֹ מְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה.
records.originEnglish: On Chanukah we light eight lamps. The eighth alludes to understanding in the heart, the source of the seven lights mentioned above: the heart’s longing and will to reach the illumination of Torah so that it spreads within the heart. The deepest yearning to attain Torah’s light was revealed in the days of the Greek decree, which sought to abolish Torah and commandments. Their hearts were greatly broken by this: it seemed that Heaven was preventing them because their Torah and commandments were not accepted before God, like a servant whose pitcher is poured back into his face. Through this they grew bitter and their hearts’ longing to study Torah in secret increased. Even those who could not hide themselves and study had an even greater cry and longing within their hearts to attain Torah’s light. Through this they merited the miracle of finding iron spits to make the menorah, the vessel receiving the light of the seven lamps. It corresponds to the will in the heart, through which a vessel is made to receive Torah’s illumination.
records.targetHebrew: מבאר בזה הזוה"ק גודל היקרות הנרמז בערבי נחל שאין בהם לא טעם ולא ריח והוא כי בכל חוזק היגיעה וגודל הסבלנות שהאדם סובל ומיגע עצמו בדברי תורה אשר באמת א"א כלל להשיג ולהגיע עד סוף תכליתה כדכתיב ארוכה מארץ מדה ואפילו אחר שמשיג האדם ברוב יגיעתו איזה חלק בד"ת בכל זאת מה יודע כדאיתא בזוה"ק (הקדמה א) כיון דשאל בר נש ומפשפש לאסתכלא ולמנדע מדרגא לדרגא עד סוף כל דרגין כיון דמטי תמן מה ידעת מה אסתכלתא מה פשפשתא הא כלא סתים כקדמיתא וכו' הרי שאי אפשר כלל להשיג ולהגיע לתכלית עומק רצונו ית' וכל מה שנפתח להאדם יותר אור בד"ת מכיר ביותר שלא התחיל עדיין להשיג בה כלום ואחר כל זאת אינו נמאם להאדם כלל לקוץ בה ח"ו אלא אדרבא כל מה שמיגע בה ביותר נתוסף בו יותר תשוקה על תשוקתו ונתחזק אצלו כל פעם הרצון והחשק ביותר חביבות ועוצם תמימות מזה מוכח אשר באותה התשוקה והרצון בעצמה כמו שהיא משוללת השגה והבנה נמצא באמת כל מיני שלימות ובאמת כל הקנין והשגה שישיגו ישראל לעתיד בדברי תורה זה הכל יהיה נמשך רק מחמת הרצון והיגיעה שהיה אצלם מקודם בזה העולם בעת שהיו עדיין משוללי השגה והבנה בד"ת הרי שיש לאותה התשוקה והיגיעה בעצמה כל השלימות גם בלעדי הפירות הנצמחים להאדם אח"כ ע"י יגיעתו
records.targetEnglish: The Zohar explains the great preciousness indicated by the river willows, which have neither taste nor fragrance. However intensely a person toils and however much difficulty he bears in Torah, he cannot reach its ultimate extent, as it says, ‘Its measure is longer than the earth.’ Even after he attains a portion of Torah through much toil, what does he know? As the Zohar says: after a person questions and searches from level to level to the end of all levels, what has he known, observed, or searched out? All is hidden as at first. One cannot reach the ultimate depth of God’s will. The more Torah light opens to a person, the more he recognizes that he has not yet begun to attain anything within it. Yet after all this it does not become repulsive to him, so that he would tire of it, Heaven forbid. On the contrary, the more he toils, the more longing is added to his longing; his will and desire continually grow stronger with greater affection and wholehearted simplicity. This proves that within that very desire and will, even while lacking attainment and understanding, every kind of completeness is truly present. All the acquisition and understanding Israel will attain in Torah in the future will come from the will and toil they previously possessed in this world, while still lacking attainment and understanding. Thus that very desire and toil possess completeness even apart from the fruits that later grow through the toil.
records.explanation: Sod explains why Rav Tzadok includes even those unable to hide and study: present achievement is not the only measure of a genuine relation to Torah. The target’s test is continued love and effort despite not seeing the desired fruit. Its full continuation contrasts that persistence with a worldly appetite that rejects the whole effort when one pleasure is missing; it does not praise chosen ignorance or refusal to learn.

records.themeTitle: Concealment can turn received light into actively sought Torah
records.themeSummary: The Second Temple’s distinctive Torah attainment is explained through the longing that follows the loss of an initially given light.
records.originHebrew: וְאִיתָא (שַׁבָּת י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳): "מִי כָּתַב מְגִלַּת תַּעֲנִית? אָמְרוּ: חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן חִזְקִיָּה וְסִיעָתוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ מְחַבְּבִין אֶת הַצָּרוֹת"; וְלִכְאוֹרָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ לוֹמַר שֶׁהָיוּ מְחַבְּבִין אֶת הַנִּסִּים, וּמַה לָּהֶם לְהַצָּרוֹת? אָמְנָם עַל יְדֵי הַצָּרוֹת וְהַגְּזֵרוֹת זָכוּ לִמְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה, וּכְמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "שִׁבְטְךָ וּמִשְׁעַנְתֶּךָ הֵמָּה יְנַחֲמֻנִי", שֶׁדַּוְקָא עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁבֶט מוּסָר בָּא לָהֶם הַמִּשְׁעֶנֶת בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת. וְכִדְאִיתָא בְּפִרְקֵי הֵיכָלוֹת (פֶּרֶק כ״ז) שֶׁבְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁרְתָה שָׁם שְׁכִינָה, אֲבָל הֲדָרָהּ, יְקָרָהּ, כְּבוֹדָהּ וּגְדֻלָּתָהּ וְכוּלֵיהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה לֹא נִתְּנָה עַד בַּיִת שֵׁנִי, עַיֵּן שָׁם; וְהַמְּכֻוָּן עַל זְמַן הַחַשְׁמוֹנָאִים שֶׁהָיָה הַתְחָלַת הֶאָרַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
records.originEnglish: Shabbat 13b says: ‘Who wrote Megillat Ta’anit? They said: Chananyah ben Chizkiyah and his circle, who cherished the troubles.’ Apparently it should have said that they cherished the miracles; what have they to do with the troubles? Yet through the troubles and decrees they merited Torah’s illumination. As it says, ‘Your rod and Your staff comfort me’: precisely through the disciplinary rod, the support came to them with greater force. Pirkei Heikhalot says that although the Divine Presence did not dwell in the Second Temple, Torah’s splendor, preciousness, honor, and greatness were not given until the Second Temple. The intention is the Hasmonean period, when the illumination of Oral Torah began.
records.targetHebrew: תְּחִלָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מֵאִיר לָאָדָם, וְהָאָדָם אֵין רָגִיל בָּזֶה עֲדַיִן וְקָשֶׁה עָלָיו לְקַבְּלוֹ כְּיָתֵד קָבוּעַ בְּמָקוֹם נֶאֱמָן שֶׁלֹּא יִמּוֹט, וּמְאַבְּדוֹ; וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָאָדָם נוֹהֶה אַחֲרָיו וּמְבַקְּשׁוֹ, וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר וּפוֹתֵחַ לוֹ, כְּטַעֲנַת "הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ וְכוּלֵי", אִם לֹא בְּקֹשִׁי גָּדוֹל, כְּעִנְיַן "כְּשֶׁרָצִיתִי לֹא רָצִיתָ, עַכְשָׁו וְכוּלֵי" (בְּרָכוֹת ז.). וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַתַּן תּוֹרָה, הָיָה בִּכְפִיַּת הַר כְּגִיגִית, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָדָר קִבְּלוּהָ בִּימֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ בְּרָצוֹן; אֲבָל לֹא נַעֲשָׂה לָהֶם נֵס בִּימֵי עֶזְרָא כְּבִימֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן, שֶׁגָּרַם הַחֵטְא כִּדְאִיתָא בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דִּבְרָכוֹת (ד.), רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר חֵטְא הַקּוֹדֵם; וְלֹא שָׁרְתָה שְׁכִינָה בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי. וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם אִיתָא בְּסוֹף סֵפֶר הֵיכָלוֹת שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּתְּנָה תּוֹרָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם כָּל מַעֲלוֹתֶיהָ, עַיֵּין שָׁם י"ז מַעֲלוֹת דְּחָשֵׁיב, לֹא הָיוּ עַד הַבַּיִת שֵׁנִי, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁרְתָה בּוֹ שְׁכִינָה. וְעַיֵּין עוֹד שָׁם אַחַר כָּךְ שֶׁלֹּא הִנִּיחוּ אֶבֶן עַל אֶבֶן בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי עַד שֶׁכָּפוּ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְגִלָּה לָהֶם רָזֵי כָּל דָּבָר, עַיֵּין שָׁם; וְ"כָפוּ" הוּא נֶגֶד כְּפִיַּת הַר כְּגִיגִית דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה [וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר דִּכְפִיָּה זוֹ הוּא בִּיטּוּל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע, שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (סט:) שֶׁהוּא נֶגֶד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וַאֲשֶׁר הֲרֵעֹתִי", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי בְּפֶרֶק אֵין עוֹמְדִין וּבְהֶחָלִיל].
records.targetEnglish: At first God illuminates for a person. The person is not yet accustomed to this, finds it difficult to receive it as a peg fixed in a secure place that will not move, and loses it. Afterwards the person yearns after it and seeks it, but God does not reopen it for him—as in the plea, ‘Return us …’—except with great difficulty, as in ‘When I wanted, you did not want; now …’. This is the giving of Torah under the mountain held over them like a tub, followed by their accepting it again willingly in Ahasuerus’s days. Yet no miracle was performed for them in Ezra’s days as in Joshua’s, because the earlier sin caused this, and the Divine Presence did not dwell in the Second Temple. Nevertheless, the end of Sefer Heikhalot says that although Torah had been given, its seventeen listed qualities were not present until the Second Temple, even though the Divine Presence did not dwell there. It further says that they did not set stone upon stone in the Second Temple until they compelled the Holy One to reveal the secrets of everything. This ‘compulsion’ corresponds to the mountain’s compulsion at the giving of Torah. One may suggest that this compulsion was the removal of the evil inclination described in Yoma 69b, contrary to God’s will, as in ‘and that which I caused to be evil,’ and as I explained elsewhere.
records.explanation: Tzidkat connects the same Second Temple/Heikhalot claim to a concrete sequence: light first received, then lost, then sought through difficulty. This explains why the origin speaks of cherishing the troubles for the Torah illumination gained through them. The quoted account is a theological interpretation of that transition, and retains the author’s tentative “one may suggest” concerning the reciprocal compulsion.

records.themeTitle: The work of hardship can lead toward joy and community
records.themeSummary: The troubles associated with receiving Torah are valued for what grows through them; their culmination need not be isolation or continuing pain.
records.originHebrew: וְאִיתָא (שַׁבָּת י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳): "מִי כָּתַב מְגִלַּת תַּעֲנִית? אָמְרוּ: חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן חִזְקִיָּה וְסִיעָתוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ מְחַבְּבִין אֶת הַצָּרוֹת"; וְלִכְאוֹרָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ לוֹמַר שֶׁהָיוּ מְחַבְּבִין אֶת הַנִּסִּים, וּמַה לָּהֶם לְהַצָּרוֹת? אָמְנָם עַל יְדֵי הַצָּרוֹת וְהַגְּזֵרוֹת זָכוּ לִמְאוֹר הַתּוֹרָה, וּכְמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "שִׁבְטְךָ וּמִשְׁעַנְתֶּךָ הֵמָּה יְנַחֲמֻנִי", שֶׁדַּוְקָא עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁבֶט מוּסָר בָּא לָהֶם הַמִּשְׁעֶנֶת בְּיֶתֶר שְׂאֵת. וְכִדְאִיתָא בְּפִרְקֵי הֵיכָלוֹת (פֶּרֶק כ״ז) שֶׁבְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁרְתָה שָׁם שְׁכִינָה, אֲבָל הֲדָרָהּ, יְקָרָהּ, כְּבוֹדָהּ וּגְדֻלָּתָהּ וְכוּלֵיהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה לֹא נִתְּנָה עַד בַּיִת שֵׁנִי, עַיֵּן שָׁם; וְהַמְּכֻוָּן עַל זְמַן הַחַשְׁמוֹנָאִים שֶׁהָיָה הַתְחָלַת הֶאָרַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה.
records.originEnglish: Shabbat 13b says: ‘Who wrote Megillat Ta’anit? They said: Chananyah ben Chizkiyah and his circle, who cherished the troubles.’ Apparently it should have said that they cherished the miracles; what have they to do with the troubles? Yet through the troubles and decrees they merited Torah’s illumination. As it says, ‘Your rod and Your staff comfort me’: precisely through the disciplinary rod, the support came to them with greater force. Pirkei Heikhalot says that although the Divine Presence did not dwell in the Second Temple, Torah’s splendor, preciousness, honor, and greatness were not given until the Second Temple. The intention is the Hasmonean period, when the illumination of Oral Torah began.
records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayechi 7
records.targetHebrew: וְהוּא שֶׁהִנִּיחַ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּשֵׁבֶט גָּד מִדַּת יִסּוּרִין כִּי זֶה הַשֵּׁבֶט אוֹמֵר כִּי בִּלְתִּי אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּכָּנְסוּ דִּבְרֵי תּוֹרָה בְּלֵב הָאָדָם בְּלֹא יִסּוּרִין, וּבְדֶרֶךְ עוֹלָם מִי שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל יִסּוּרִין אֵין לוֹ כָּל כָּךְ שִׂמְחָה וְאֵינוֹ כָּל כָּךְ בְּצַוְותָּא עִם בְּנֵי אָדָם. וְלָכֵן נִתְבָּרְכוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָהֶם שִׂמְחָה וְצַוְותָּא, וּבֵרֵךְ אוֹתָם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָהֶם הִתְחַבְּרוּת וְיִהְיֶה בָּהֶם גְּדוּדִים גְּדוּדִים, וְלָכֵן לֹא נִמְצָא בְּשׁוּם שֵׁבֶט שֶׁיִּכְלוֹל כָּל הַמִּסְפָּרִים הַיְינוּ מֵאוֹת וַאֲלָפִים וַעֲשָׂרוֹת רַק בְּשֵׁבֶט גָּד מַה שֶּׁאֵינוֹ בִּשְׁאָר הַשְּׁבָטִים, "וְהוּא יָגֻד עָקֵב" הַיְינוּ בִּזְמַן שֶׁיִּצְטָרֵךְ לְקַבֵּץ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל אָז הוּא יֶאֱגוֹד וְיִקְשׁוֹר אֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל, וּמִמֶּנּוּ יָבֹא כָּל מִינֵי שִׂמְחָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, כִּי אֵלִיָּהוּ הוּא מִשֵּׁבֶט גָּד כַּנִּזְכָּר בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה עַיִן אָלֶף, יוֹד בֵּית).
records.targetEnglish: God placed the attribute of suffering in Gad’s tribe. This tribe says that it is impossible for words of Torah to enter the human heart without suffering. Ordinarily, a person who suffers does not have much joy and does not have much companionship with others. Therefore they were blessed to possess joy and companionship: he blessed them with connection, that they should form groups upon groups. Thus only in Gad’s tribe do all the numerical orders—hundreds, thousands, and tens—appear together in its enumeration, unlike the other tribes. ‘He will press upon the heel’ means that when Israel needs to be gathered, he will bind and join all Israel, and from him will come every kind of joy to Israel, for Elijah is from Gad’s tribe, as stated in the Midrash.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach identifies hardship as Gad’s particular path of Torah and then specifically repairs its ordinary tendency toward loneliness and diminished joy. This develops the origin’s idea that the “rod” becomes a greater “support.” The claim that Torah requires suffering remains attributed to this tribe’s perspective in the target; it is not generalized into a direction for every person to seek hardship.

records.themeTitle: The unwritten miracle marks growth from an already given seed
records.themeSummary: The Written/Oral Torah distinction is explained through receiving an initial reality and drawing further understanding from what has already been given.
records.originHebrew: דַּחֲנֻכָּה הַתְחָלַת הַנִּסִּים שֶׁלֹּא נִתְּנוּ לִכָּתֵב, כִּי אֶסְתֵּר הוּא סוֹף הַנִּסִּים שֶׁנִּתְּנוּ לִכָּתֵב (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יוֹמָא כ״ט עַמּוּד א׳), וְהַיְנוּ הַתְחָלַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה; כִּי הִיא הַתְחָלַת מִצְוָה דְּרַבָּנָן שֶׁהוּא רַק מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא עַל בִּרְכַּת נֵר חֲנֻכָּה: "וְהֵיכָן צִוָּנוּ? מִ'לֹּא תָסוּר'".
records.originEnglish: Chanukah is the beginning of the miracles not given to be written, since Esther is the end of the miracles given to be written, as in Yoma 29a. This is the beginning of Oral Torah: it is the beginning of a rabbinic commandment rooted solely in Oral Torah, as the Talmud asks concerning the Chanukah-lamp blessing, ‘Where did He command us?’—from ‘Do not depart from what they tell you.’
records.targetRef: Likkutei Maamarim, Upon Completion of Talmud 11
records.targetHebrew: וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב הוּא יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן מַה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא יֵשׁ מִיֵּשׁ שֶׁכְּבָר הָיָה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְהוּא מֵבִין דָּבָר מִתּוֹךְ דָּבָר לְחַדֵּשׁ, וְכֵן נֵס דַּחֲנוּכָּה שֶׁהָיָה כְּבָר שֶׁמֶן מוּעָט דְּהַייְנוּ יֵשׁ מִיֵּשׁ וְלֹא יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן הַגָּמוּר
records.targetEnglish: Written Torah is something from nothing. Oral Torah is something from something: Written Torah already existed, and the person understands one matter from another to innovate. So too Chanukah’s miracle: a little oil already existed; it was something from something, not absolutely something from nothing.
records.explanation: Likkutei explains the origin’s classification through the form of Torah’s growth: Oral Torah draws new understanding from an existing gift. The small oil supply makes that distinction concrete. “Not given to be written” is used here as a division of revelatory eras and kinds of miracle, not as a claim that Oral Torah can never later appear in written books.

records.themeTitle: Torah gives counsel while the heart is still being refined
records.themeSummary: Toil in darkness can be understood as entering Torah’s protection and learning concrete discipline of action, judgment, and the heart.
records.originHebrew: וְכִדְאִיתָא (תַּנְחוּמָא נֹחַ ג׳) שֶׁעַל עַמְלֵי תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נֶאֱמַר: "הָעָם הַהֹלְכִים בַּחֹשֶׁךְ רָאוּ אוֹר גָּדוֹל" אוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן וְכוּלֵיהּ; וְגַם לֹא כָּפָה הָהָר כְּגִיגִית רַק עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, לְפִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ צַעַר גָּדוֹל וּנְדוּד שֵׁנָה וּמְנַבֵּל עַצְמוֹ עָלֶיהָ. וְעַל לִמּוּד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נֶאֱמַר: "וְאָהַבְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכָל נַפְשְׁךָ וּבְכָל מְאֹדֶךָ", שֶׁאֵין זוֹכֶה לַהּ רַק מִי שֶׁהוּא אוֹהֵב הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּכָל לִבּוֹ וּבְכָל נַפְשׁוֹ וּבְכָל מְאֹדוֹ, עַיֵּן שָׁם; וַעֲלֵיהֶם נֶאֱמַר: "וְאֹהֲבָיו כְּצֵאת הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ בִּגְבֻרָתוֹ", שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵאִיר עֵינֵיהֶם לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא.
records.originEnglish: The Tanchuma says that concerning those who toil in Oral Torah it is written, ‘The people walking in darkness saw a great light’—the first light. The mountain was held over them like a tub only for Oral Torah, because it involves great difficulty, loss of sleep, and making oneself unsightly over it. Concerning the study of Oral Torah it is written, ‘You shall love … with all your heart, all your soul, and all your might,’ for it is attained only by one who loves the Holy One with all his heart, soul, and might. Concerning them it says, ‘Those who love Him are like the sun going forth in its strength’: the Holy One illuminates their eyes in the future.
records.targetRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Noach 1
records.targetHebrew: אֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדוֹת נֹחַ וְכוּלֵי עֲשֵׂה לְךָ תֵּבַת עֲצֵי גֹפֶר וְכוּלֵי. עִנְיַן הַתֵּבָה, שֶׁנָּתַן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עֵצָה וַהֲגָנָה לְנֹחַ עַד שֶׁעָבְרוּ יְמֵי הַזַּעַם, וְכֵן לְכׇל מִי שֶׁלֹּא נִזְדַּכֵּךְ לִבּוֹ עֲדַיִן יוּכַל לִלְמוֹד עֵצוֹת אֵיךְ יִסָּתֵר עַצְמוֹ וְיָגֵן בַּעֲדוֹ מִכׇּל רָע הַמִּתְרַגֵּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם, וְכֵן אָמְרוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תַּנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ו): אִם רוֹאֶה אָדָם שֶׁיִּסּוּרִין בָּאִין עָלָיו יָרוּץ לְחַדְרֵי חֲדָרִים שֶׁל תּוֹרָה וְהִיא נוֹתֶנֶת לוֹ עֵצָה אֵיךְ לְהִנָּצֵל. וְעִנְיַן הַתֵּבָה הוּא עַל פִּי מַה דְּאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (פְּסָחִים קיג:): שְׁלוֹשָׁה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אוֹהֲבָן: מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ כּוֹעֵס, וְאֵינוֹ מִשְׁתַּכֵּר, וּמִי שֶׁמַּעֲבִיר עַל מִדּוֹתָיו. מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ כּוֹעֵס הַיְינוּ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַרְאֶה שׁוּם כַּעַס בְּפוֹעַל, וְאֵינוֹ מִשְׁתַּכֵּר הַיְינוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ יִשּׁוּב הַדַּעַת וּמַכִּיר וּמַאֲמִין בְּבוֹרֵא עוֹלָם, וּמִי שֶׁמַּעֲבִיר עַל מִדּוֹתָיו הַיְינוּ שֶׁמֵּסִיר הַכַּעַס גַּם מִלִּבּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בְּלִבּוֹ שׁוּם תַּרְעוֹמוֹת עַל חֲבֵרוֹ.
records.targetEnglish: ‘These are Noah’s generations … Make yourself an ark of gopher wood …’. The ark means that God gave Noah counsel and protection until the days of wrath had passed. Likewise anyone whose heart is not yet refined can learn counsels for sheltering himself and protecting himself from all the evil stirring in the world. Thus the Sages said: if a person sees sufferings coming upon him, let him run to the innermost chambers of Torah, and it gives him counsel for escape. The ark’s meaning follows the Talmud’s saying that the Holy One loves three: one who does not become angry, one who does not become drunk, and one who overlooks offenses. One who does not become angry does not show anger in action. One who does not become drunk possesses a settled mind and recognizes and believes in the Creator of the world. One who overlooks offenses removes anger even from his heart, so that no grievance against his fellow remains in his heart.
records.explanation: Mei HaShiloach supplies practical content for Torah’s role amid trouble: the learner is still being refined, and the counsel reaches outward action, settled understanding, and the removal of resentment. The origin stresses the arduous love required for Oral Torah; the target explains how entering Torah under pressure can shape the heart, without promising that merely accumulating information removes suffering.

records.themeTitle: Wholehearted acceptance makes Oral Torah an entrusted possession
records.themeSummary: The permanent inheritance of Oral Torah is connected to accepting its work willingly, after the original coercion.
records.originHebrew: כִּי מִיָּד בְּהַתְחָלַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה הָיָה בִּתְשׁוּקָה גְּדוֹלָה, כְּמַה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיִּחַן שָׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל" "כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד בְּלֵב אֶחָד", וְזֶה הָיָה עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב, שֶׁעַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה נִצְרַךְ לִכְפּוֹת עֲלֵיהֶם הַהַר כְּגִיגִית כִּדְאִיתָא בְּתַנְחוּמָא; אֲבָל אַחַר זֶה הָדַר קִבְּלוּהָ מֵאַהֲבָה בִּימֵי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ, וּבִטְּלוּ הַמּוֹדָעָה דִּכְפִיַּת הָהָר כְּגִיגִית.
records.originEnglish: At the very beginning of the giving of Torah there was great longing, as it says, ‘Israel encamped there’—‘like one person with one heart.’ This concerned Written Torah. For Oral Torah, the mountain had to be held over them like a tub, as in the Tanchuma. Afterwards, however, they accepted it again out of love in Ahasuerus’s days and annulled the protest arising from the mountain’s coercion.
records.targetHebrew: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפִרְקֵי הֵיכָלוֹת (פֶּרֶק כ״ז): דְּאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁרְתָה שְׁכִינָה בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי, מִכָּל מָקוֹם עִיקַּר הַתּוֹרָה וְזִיוָהּ וַהֲדָרָהּ לֹא הָיָה אֶלָּא בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי, שֶׁלֹּא רָצוּ לִבְנוֹת עַד שֶׁהִבְטִיחָם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְגַלּוֹת לָהֶם רָזֵי הַתּוֹרָה, יְעֻיַּן שָׁם בִּפְנִים. וְהַיְינוּ כִּי הַתְחָלַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הָיָה בְּבַיִת שֵׁנִי מֵאַנְשֵׁי כְּנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה, שֶׁהֵם מְיַסְּדֵי הַבַּיִת, הֵם יִסְּדוּ גַּם כֵּן הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי דִּשְׁקָלִים (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ה׳). וּבִימֵי מָרְדֳּכַי, דְּקִיְּמוּ מַה שֶּׁקִּבְּלוּ כְּבָר, שֶׁחָזְרוּ לְקַבֵּל הַתּוֹרָה מֵאַהֲבָה שֶׁלֹּא עַל יְדֵי כְּפִיַּת הַר כְּגִיגִית, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת פ״ח עַמּוּד א׳), אָז זָכוּ לְכָךְ. כִּי עִיקַּר הַכְּפִיַּת הַר הָיָה עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנְחוּמָא פָּרָשַׁת נֹחַ, עַיֵּן שָׁם בִּפְנִים; וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא קִבְּלוּהָ מֵרְצוֹנָם, לֹא נִמְסְרָה עֲדַיִן לָהֶם לְגַמְרֵי, וְהָיוּ מִתְנַהֲגִים עַל פִּי נְבִיאִים, הַכֹּל בִּכְתָב מִיַּד ה'.
records.targetEnglish: Pirkei Heikhalot says that although the Divine Presence did not dwell in the Second Temple, the essential Torah and its radiance and splendor were only in the Second Temple. They did not wish to build until God promised to reveal Torah’s secrets to them. For Oral Torah began in the Second Temple with the Men of the Great Assembly: those who founded the Temple also founded Oral Torah, as stated in Yerushalmi Shekalim. In Mordechai’s days, when they confirmed what they had already received and accepted Torah again out of love rather than through the mountain’s coercion, they merited this. The essential coercion concerned Oral Torah, as stated in Tanchuma Noach. As long as they had not accepted it willingly, it had not yet been completely entrusted to them, and they conducted themselves through prophets, everything in writing from God’s hand.
records.explanation: Resisei states what voluntary acceptance changes: Oral Torah becomes completely entrusted to its human recipients. This supplies the mechanism linking Rav Tzadok’s account of renewed love to a light that remains as an inheritance, rather than treating the change as only a stronger emotion.
